article_content: Washington (CNN) -- Even though Republican party leaders were meeting in Washington this week, Hillary Clinton's presence was strongly felt. Is there a secret support from Obama for Hillary Clinton in 2016? In conversations between Republican National Committee meetings, the former secretary of state's name was frequently mentioned. At a rules committee meeting on Thursday night, Clinton -- the presumed front-runner for the Democratic presidential nomination in 2016 -- was alluded to as 'she who should not be named.' And at the most-watched events, Republicans vowed a laser-like focus on reclaiming the White House in 2016. It seems that while some Democrats are trying to prevent the coronation of Clinton as their inevitable presidential candidate, most Republican figures in Washington admitted they believe that all roads to the White House involve Clinton. 'I think it is the most realistic assessment,' said Steve Duprey, national committeeman from New Hampshire. 'It is a party of one giant and a bunch of elves who might be running against her.' 'She has a political organization, she has the history, she has respect from being a senator, first lady, secretary of state. I think it is just prudent for the Republicans to assume she is the nominee, and frankly, I think it helps focus people,' he added. A major Obama group will now advocate for Hillary Clinton. And Republicans are correct in their assessment of Clinton's front-runner status -- Clinton has consistently led in every poll taken about Democrats for 2016. In the latest Quinnipiac University poll, 65% of Democrats stated Clinton would be their choice for the nomination. Vice President Joe Biden was second with 8%, a substantial 57 points behind. 'Virtually none of the other Democrats could beat her,' said Saul Anuzis, the former chairman of the Michigan Republican Party. 'Now, many things could happen, but I think most Republicans assume we are going to run against her.' Since leaving the State Department in 2013, the former secretary of state has maintained an active schedule, earning paychecks on the corporate speaking circuit and receiving awards at ceremonies across the country. Hillary Clinton is scheduled for a California swing in April. Democratic groups have begun aligning themselves behind her possible candidacy in 2016. In addition to groups like Ready for Hillary and Emily's List -- two pro-Clinton fundraising organizations -- the liberal Priorities USA moved this week to support Clinton and announced they will begin raising significant funds to help elect Clinton to the White House. The key issue: Clinton has publicly stated she is still considering whether to run for president. Late last year, Clinton said she would decide whether to run or not by the end of this year. In promoting Clinton as the inevitable candidate, Republicans have both praised her -- 'She has a first-rate organization,' Duprey said -- and tested out potential attack strategies. 'We are doing everything we can to define her early,' Matt Moore, chairman of the South Carolina Republican Party, said about Clinton, who he described as the 'mother of Obamacare.' 'She is an opportunistic person who has been running for president for 20 years.' Moore said the ability to focus on Clinton almost three years before election day means that the narrative Republicans will push has more time to gain traction. Moore sees a parallel between Clinton in 2016 and Mitt Romney, the Republican nominee in 2012. 'The trouble we had in 2012 was that our nominee was defined really early over a five- or six-year period, and it was hard to break through these presuppositions,' he said. He added that, for that reason, Republicans 'are preparing in South Carolina and elsewhere as if she is the nominee.' Clinton cover receives buzz and criticism. article_content: Marine Le Pen, the former leader of France's far-right National Rally, has been found guilty of defaming Cimade, an NGO that aids migrants, refugees, and asylum seekers by providing legal assistance. During a BFMTV interview in January 2022, Le Pen, who stepped down as leader of the National Rally in November of the same year, accused Cimade of 'sometimes' being 'accomplices of smugglers' involved in an 'illegal immigration network from the Comoros' in Mayotte. Mayotte is a French overseas department situated in the Indian Ocean between Mozambique and Madagascar. When a reporter asked, 'Are humanitarian associations complicit in the crime of entry?', Le Pen responded, 'Sometimes yes. They are even complicit with smugglers,' before singling out Cimade. She stated, 'Cimade actually organises the illegal immigration network coming from the Comoros' in Mayotte. At the time, Le Pen was a candidate in the April 2022 presidential election, which Emmanuel Macron won. Le Pen achieved her highest first-round score in Mayotte, attributable to her emphasis on illegal immigration. On Friday, a French court convicted her of defamation for her statement regarding Cimade and ordered her to pay the NGO a suspended fine of €500. She must also pay €2,000 in court costs and €1 in damages. The court stated that Le Pen's remarks 'exceeded the permissible dose of exaggeration in the context in which they were uttered'. 'The limits of freedom of expression (have) been crossed,' the court declared.

article_content: England's national team faces a challenge in competing at the World Cup, despite the lucrative Premier League. With just two months until the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, manager Roy Hodgson discussed squad selection challenges. The Premier League has flourished, attracting global stars, but English football's national team has struggled. The Three Lions have reached the semifinals only once since their 1966 World Cup victory on home soil. Hodgson may have to select players who aren't regular starters for their clubs. He noted that nearly 30% of the squad might consist of players not regularly featured in their first teams. Hodgson remarked that this situation would have been 'unthinkable' in the past. A survey indicated that just over a third of Premier League players are eligible to represent England. Injuries to Theo Walcott and Jay Rodriguez have further reduced Hodgson's player pool. Despite emerging talents like Ross Barkley, Raheem Sterling, and Luke Shaw, England may rely on younger players. Hodgson acknowledged a 'transitional period' requiring adaptation. He explained that young players face competition from top foreign talent at top clubs. England faced criticism after a second-round exit in South Africa in 2010 following a defeat by Germany. Fabio Capello previously stated that England struggles at the World Cup due to excessive games. Hodgson concedes some truth to Capello's point but denies that tiredness will undermine their Brazil chances. Hodgson acknowledged the intensive nature of the Premier League but aims to manage it. He emphasized accepting the situation and avoiding excuses. Hodgson suggested tailoring training based on individual player fatigue levels. He concluded by stating that such considerations have likely occurred in the past and aren't a guaranteed solution.

article_content: Researchers have discovered that the SARS outbreak, responsible for 774 deaths, originated in Chinese Horseshoe bats. Scientists identified two SARS coronaviruses (SARS-CoV) in these bats, noting their close similarity to the virus that infected humans. The Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) pandemic resulted in approximately 10% mortality among the 8,094 individuals infected during 2002 and 2003. The outbreak may have stemmed from wildlife markets where bats were kept or from human populations living near bat caves. Chinese Rufous Horseshoe bats, recognized by the horseshoe-shaped structure on their noses, are found across China, India, Nepal, and Vietnam. Scientists' analysis revealed that the viruses found in these bats can infect human cells directly, indicating a potential transmission pathway. The Sars-like coronavirus exhibits around 95% genetic similarity to the Sars virus affecting humans. Reported in the journal Nature, these findings ‘definitively confirm’ bats as the source of the virus. Researchers emphasize the importance of safeguarding bat habitats to prevent their migration into densely populated urban areas in search of food. Professor Shi Zhengli from the Chinese Academy of Sciences in Beijing led the research team that found viruses in these bats infect human cells in the same way.

article_content: A young girl named Ella Hansen, five years old and from Wirral, Merseyside, has found relief from her severe epilepsy, which once caused over 1,000 seizures daily, through a diet rich in cream and cheese. Ella adheres to a ketogenic diet, which is high in fats such as cheese, cream, butter, and oil. This diet helps manage her epilepsy by forcing her body to burn fats instead of carbohydrates for energy. Since starting this diet in May, Ella's condition has dramatically improved, reducing her seizures to fewer than ten per day. Before the diet, her mother described her as being 'like a zombie,' but now she's active and playful. Her mother, Zara, hopes Ella will be seizure-free within six months and eventually be able to discontinue the diet in a few years. She acknowledges the strangeness of feeding her child so much fat but considers it a 'miracle.' Ella's diet includes items like smoothies with extra cream, humus with extra oil, and toast with plenty of butter. Despite common perceptions about fat, Zara emphasizes that fat is changing Ella's life. The ketogenic diet induces a state called ketosis, where the body burns fats for fuel. While the exact reason for seizure reduction is unclear, the diet has significantly enhanced Ella's quality of life. Zara noticed Ella's condition when she began falling behind other children. Now, there's a possibility she may attend a mainstream school in the future. Ella's ketogenic diet is carefully calculated to ensure she receives proper nourishment while controlling her seizures. Her favorite snack is toast with lots of butter and sugar-free maple syrup. Zara also gets high-fat cuts of meat from the butcher and prepares keto muffins and fat bombs for Ella. She urges other parents to consider the diet, emphasizing that it has given them 'their daughter back.' Emma Williams MBE, founder of Matthew's Friends Charity, supports the use of ketogenic diets for children and highlights the shift in thinking required to embrace a 'fat is good' mentality. Matthew's Friends emphasizes the importance of medical supervision for ketogenic diets and supports families in using them. Zara stated, 'Matthew's Friends were amazing and really helped us out. They were a great support network, especially during the early stages of the diet.' The plan is that soon Ella will be seizure free, drug free, and eventually she'll be able to come off the diet within the next few years. Zara had noticed Ella was falling behind other children her age. She said: 'Ella had been doing perfectly as a baby but then stopped hitting her milestones. 'She was very late at crawling and she didn't walk until she was almost two. '

article_content: Stoke City's midfielder, Wilson Palacios, shared how the tragic loss of his younger brother to armed kidnappers fuels his commitment to combat gang culture. Back in 2007, while Palacios was playing for Birmingham City, his 14-year-old brother, Edwin, was abducted from their family home in Honduras by a criminal gang and found deceased 19 months later. 'A gang stole my brother from us. They demanded money, which we paid, but he was never returned,' Palacios revealed to the Daily Star. The Stoke midfielder admitted he contemplated retiring from football after this devastating loss. 'It was heartbreaking. It profoundly impacted my life, and I resolved that no other child should endure such suffering.' Since then, the former Tottenham player has dedicated himself to preventing gang-related crimes. His latest initiative involves partnering with the coffee company, Kenco. The 'Coffee vs Gangs' program seeks to assist 20 vulnerable young people at risk of gang involvement by providing educational and training opportunities to become coffee business owners. Honduras faces a severe crisis, marked by the world's highest murder rate, averaging 20 killings daily. Drug trafficking, widespread gang violence, and poverty exacerbate the situation. Palacios actively supports Kenco's Coffee vs Gangs project to empower young individuals in his native country. The program is designed to offer these young people a chance to thrive as coffee entrepreneurs. 'In the aftermath of the kidnapping, I considered giving up football. However, I understood that my brother would have wanted me to continue playing.' 'He had a passion for football. Therefore, our family collectively decided that I should pursue my career,' Palacios disclosed. The 30-year-old named his son Edwin to honor his brother's memory. Wilson Palacios champions Kenco's Coffee vs Gangs project. To discover more, visit www.coffeevsgangs.com.

article_content: The Florida Supreme Court has revoked the law license of Ana Gardiner, a former judge, due to an inappropriate 'personal and emotional relationship' with a prosecutor. This relationship began while she was presiding over a death penalty case where the prosecutor was involved. The seven justices of the Supreme Court were unanimous in their decision to increase the punishment initially suggested by a hearing officer, who had proposed a one-year suspension for Judge Gardiner. The court emphasized that such a serious ethical breach, particularly in a capital case that led to a death sentence being changed to life imprisonment, along with her initial attempts to minimize her involvement with Assistant State Attorney Howard Scheinberg, warranted her disbarment. Gardiner's disbarment officially ends her career in the legal profession after failing to disclose her intimate connection with homicide prosecutor Howard Scheinberg during a murder trial he led in 2007. During the 2007 trial where Ana Gardiner was the judge, Howard Scheinberg, then 53, engaged in frequent communication with her, including 949 phone calls and 471 text messages, resulting in his suspension from legal practice for two years. Omar Loureiro was being tried for the stabbing death of James Lentry, 57, which occurred in Lighthouse Point on New Year's Day in 2001. After Gardiner initially sentenced him to death in 2007, it was uncovered that she had a relationship with Howard Scheinberg, the case's lead prosecutor. This revelation led to Loureiro being granted a new trial, where he received a life sentence. The court noted that Gardiner had an unplanned meeting with Scheinberg at a restaurant during Loureiro's murder trial in 2007, and they later socialized at a bar. Records showed that between March 23, shortly before the guilty verdict, and August 24, when she imposed the death sentence, Gardiner and Scheinberg had extensive communication via phone calls and texts. Loureiro's defense centered on claims that Lentry had made unwanted sexual advances towards him. The investigation by the Judicial Qualifications Commission, which started in 2008, revealed that Gardiner had not been truthful about the nature of her relationship with Scheinberg during Loureiro's trial. It was only during a later investigation by the Broward state attorney that Gardiner admitted to her 'ongoing emotional relationship' with Scheinberg. Reports from The Sun Sentinel indicated that the relationship was not romantic. Ana Gardiner stepped down from her position at the Broward Circuit Court in 2010 after an 11-year tenure. She now has a month to finalize matters at her Fort Lauderdale law office following her disbarment. Gardiner has been a Florida Bar member since 1988. The Bar stated she misled the Judicial Qualifications Commission regarding the extent of her contact with Scheinberg between March and August 2007. In 2013, she married David Bogenschutz, who represented her during the Scheinberg investigation. Scheinberg's law license was suspended for two years and reinstated in 2015. After the relationship between Gardiner and Scheinberg was revealed, Loureiro's death sentence was overturned, and he was resentenced to life in prison. The Supreme Court order stated, 'Considering Gardiner's dishonest actions and the harm they caused to the administration of justice in a capital first-degree murder case, we find that disbarment is the necessary action.' The court also ordered her to cover $8,117.18 in costs.

article_content: Following his defeat in the 200-meter sprint at the London Paralympic Games, South African athlete Oscar Pistorius, known as the 'Blade Runner,' has issued an apology for the timing of his remarks regarding the length of his competitors' prosthetic limbs. He had expressed these concerns after a surprising loss to Alan Fonteles Cardaso Oliveira, a 20-year-old Brazilian runner. Shortly after the race, Pistorius had alleged that Oliveira, along with other participants, were using 'unbelievably long' prosthetic blades. He suggested that the differing stride lengths created an unfair competitive environment, acknowledging his best effort despite feeling disadvantaged. Pistorius released a statement early Monday, retracting the timing of his complaints, while affirming his conviction that a legitimate issue persists. He stated that it was inappropriate to voice his concerns immediately after the race, recognizing Oliveira's victory and extending his respect. Oliveira surpassed Pistorius in the final moments, securing the gold medal with a time of 21.45 seconds. Though slower than Pistorius' own world record of 21.30 seconds set during the qualifying heat, it was sufficient to defeat the favored Pistorius, who finished with a time of 21.52 seconds. Both athletes are double-amputees and use prosthetic limbs. Pistorius initially questioned Oliveira's remarkable comeback near the race's conclusion, expressing disbelief at the speed gained in the final stretch. He mentioned that he typically runs at just over 10 meters per second, finding Oliveira's recovery from an eight-meter deficit difficult to comprehend. Pistorius also implicated American bronze medalist Blake Leeper, suggesting that Leeper had potentially altered his blades to be longer. He claimed Leeper's knee height was significantly higher than it should be. Pistorius mentioned his previous attempts to discuss blade length with the IPC, but indicated his concerns were not addressed. The IPC responded with a statement asserting that all prostheses were measured before the race and complied with established rules. Oliveira voiced his disappointment at being accused of cheating by Pistorius, whom he regards as an idol. He affirmed that his performance was due to training and adherence to IPC regulations. Leeper supported Oliveira's claims, emphasizing his intensive training and compliance with IPC rules. He disagreed with Pistorius' assessment that the prosthetic limbs were the determining factor. Craig Spence, the IPC's director, indicated that a meeting would be arranged between Pistorius and Peter Van Der Vliet, the committee's science and medical director, to discuss his concerns calmly. The IPC acknowledged Pistorius' significant contribution to promoting Paralympic Sport. Pistorius seemingly walked back his initial statements, posting a photo of himself congratulating Oliveira on his victory, acknowledging the impressive final sprint. Prior to the Paralympics, Pistorius had achieved a milestone by becoming the first double-amputee to compete in the able-bodied Summer Olympics in London. Although he did not win a medal, his participation was celebrated as a symbol of triumph over adversity. Pistorius had previously overcome obstacles to compete against able-bodied athletes, assembling a legal team to prove that his prosthetic limbs did not give him an advantage. He had both legs amputated below the knee at 11 months due to a congenital condition and uses specialized carbon-fiber limbs. Pistorius is scheduled to participate in the men's T44 100-meter and T44 400-meter races, events he won at the Beijing Paralympics.

Pistorius aparentemente voltou atrás em suas declarações iniciais, postando uma foto de si mesmo parabenizando Oliveira por sua vitória, reconhecendo o impressionante sprint final. Antes das Paralimpíadas, Pistorius alcançou um marco ao se tornar o primeiro amputado duplo a competir nas Olimpíadas de Verão para atletas não deficientes em Londres. Ele teve ambas as pernas amputadas abaixo do joelho aos 11 meses devido a uma condição congênita e usa próteses de fibra de carbono especializadas. article_content: A notorious 1896 Wild West killing may have been solved after an amateur historian discovered a bullet fired during the shootout over a century later. The bullet was matched to the gun of one of the men who had been pardoned for the crime. Mormon sheepherders David Cummins, 22, and John Wilson, 25, were shot dead while camping in South Hills, Idaho, during a conflict between sheepherders and local ranchers. The prime suspect in the shooting, which shocked Idaho, was local gunman 'Diamondfield Jack' Davis. He was convicted but faced execution seven times before being pardoned. Eventually, two cattle company employees confessed to the crime, claiming self-defense. Now, a bullet fired over 100 years ago has been found and matched to the gun, resembling CSI-style detective work. The re-examination of the case began with local lawmaker Max Black's interest in 'Diamondfield Jack' Davis, a notorious Idaho outlaw. Davis, a flamboyant local character, was hired by the Sparks Harrell Cattle Co. to deter sheepherders from using the company's land by harassing and threatening them. An earlier incident where Davis wounded a sheepherder made him the main suspect in the deaths of Cummins and Wilson. Davis was convicted and sentenced to death but avoided execution seven times with his lawyer, James Hawley's help, until his pardon in 1902 after two other Sparks Harrell employees confessed. Black told the Idaho Statesman about his historical searches, like the Virginia farmhouse porch where General J.E.B. Stuart lost his hat in 1862. 'I couldn’t find anyone who knew exactly where this took place,' Black told the Times-News. 'Then I wondered about the court records.' Black became captivated by the Diamondfield Jack case and the sheepherders and wanted to see where Cummins and Wilson were shot. Case notes indicated that a bullet fired by James Bower, one of the confessors (Jeff Gray admitted to firing the fatal shots), pierced a saddle on a sagebrush but was never recovered. Bower testified that he lost his Colt Frontiersman .44 caliber firearm after the shootout. Black had a hunch the missing bullet remained at the scene. With an engineer friend's help, Black studied the case notes and located the likely shooting site near Deep Creek in eastern Twin Falls County. Using a metal detector, Black searched the area and found a bullet confirmed to be from a Colt Frontiersman .44, produced between 1880 and 1905, the same type Bower used. After discovering the bullet near Deep Creek, Black updated his friend, Dan Buchwitz, who realized he might have the gun. 'Max,' he said, according to the Idaho Statesman. 'I think I have that gun!' Buchwitz had received a Colt Frontiersman .44 as a gift from friends who found it in the Deep Creek area in the 1960s or '70s. The gun was unloaded, suggesting it had been fired before being lost or abandoned by Bower. Only 2,100 Colt Frontiersman pistols were ever made, increasing the likelihood it belonged to Bower. 'Diamondfield Jack' Davis was eventually pardoned and became wealthy in Nevada, founding mining towns, but his name remained linked to the murder. He survived being shot in the mouth in a bar fight and a false report of his death in the Mexican Revolution. He died after being hit by a taxi in Las Vegas in 1949. The admitted killers were acquitted for self-defense. After four years of research, Black will publish his findings in 'Diamondfield: Finding the Real Jack Davis' this summer and continue investigating 'Diamondfield Jack' Davis's life.

Com a ajuda de um amigo engenheiro, Black estudou as notas do caso e localizou o provável local do tiroteio perto de Deep Creek, no leste do condado de Twin Falls. Usando um detector de metais, Black vasculhou a área e encontrou uma bala confirmada como sendo de um Colt Frontiersman .44, produzido entre 1880 e 1905, o mesmo tipo usado por Bower. Depois de descobrir a bala perto de Deep Creek, Black atualizou seu amigo, Dan Buchwitz, que percebeu que poderia ter a arma. 'Max', disse ele, de acordo com o Idaho Statesman. 'Eu acho que tenho essa arma!' Buchwitz recebeu um Colt Frontiersman .44 de presente de amigos que o encontraram na área de Deep Creek nas décadas de 1960 ou 70. A arma estava descarregada, sugerindo que havia sido disparada antes de ser perdida ou abandonada por Bower. Apenas 2.100 pistolas Colt Frontiersman foram fabricadas, aumentando a probabilidade de que pertencesse a Bower. 'Diamondfield Jack' Davis foi eventualmente perdoado e ficou rico em Nevada, fundando cidades de mineração, mas seu nome permaneceu ligado ao assassinato. Ele sobreviveu a um tiro na boca em uma briga de bar e a uma notícia falsa de sua morte na Revolução Mexicana. Ele morreu depois de ser atropelado por um táxi em Las Vegas em 1949. Os assassinos confessos foram absolvidos por legítima defesa. Após quatro anos de pesquisa, Black publicará suas descobertas em 'Diamondfield: Finding the Real Jack Davis' neste verão e continuará investigando a vida de 'Diamondfield Jack' Davis.

article_content: Due to his refusal to endorse a ceasefire in Gaza, Labour councillors have urged Sir Keir Starmer to step down as party leader. Afrasiab Anwar, the leader of Burnley Council, and Asjad Mahmood, who leads Pendle Borough Council, stated they were speaking for Labour councillors in their respective areas. Mr Anwar claimed that Sir Keir had 'not championed Labour's core beliefs.' Sir Keir responded that his primary focus concerning the Middle East was easing suffering, not addressing calls for his resignation from within the party. Israel commenced its operations in Gaza following Hamas's killing of over 1,400 individuals in Israel and the abduction of more than 200 others on October 7. Since then, it has conducted numerous air and artillery strikes, with its ground offensive ongoing. According to the Hamas-controlled health ministry in Gaza, more than 9,000 people have died since October 7. Mr Anwar mentioned that he and his colleagues had 'witnessed the heartbreaking loss of individuals, including young children, in Palestine.' He added that 'simply mirroring Rishi Sunak's stance' was 'unacceptable to both us and the residents we represent.' Mr Mahmood stated that Mr Starmer had 'neglected to heed' appeals for a ceasefire to 'halt the needless loss of life.' He further suggested that Mr Starmer should resign to 'allow a more compassionate leader to guide our party, someone who actively opposes injustice and the indiscriminate killing of innocent individuals.' Burnley Council consists of 22 Labour councillors, while Pendle Borough Council has nine. These calls follow Sobia Malik's resignation from the Labour party; she represents Burnley Central East on Lancashire County Council. Ms Malik, now an independent councillor, cited Mr Starmer's 'profound inability' to 'display empathy or compassion, let alone condemn potential war crimes, as making her continued membership untenable.' 'I will always hold affection for the Labour Party and its values, but I can no longer reconcile these values with the current leadership's position,' she added. The Labour party has experienced numerous resignations in councils throughout England because of its Gaza stance, notably in Oxford, where it has lost control of the city council. Andy McDonald, the MP for Middlesbrough, has also been suspended from the Labour party after the party deemed his comments regarding the Israel-Gaza conflict as 'deeply offensive.' When questioned about the calls for his resignation, Sir Keir stated: 'My priority is easing the immense suffering of everyone affected by the recent events.' 'Regardless of individual opinions within my party, that is not my main concern.' He asserted that a humanitarian pause was the 'only viable approach' to achieving this. 'To demand that a sovereign nation relinquish its right to self-defense when 200 of its civilians are being held hostage is, in my view, not the correct stance,' he continued. 'Recent images clearly demonstrate what Hamas's position is on this matter.' Labour stated that the party had condemned Hamas's actions and 'emphasized the necessity of alleviating humanitarian suffering in Gaza,' but affirmed Israel's right to 'prevent Hamas from perpetrating such terrorist acts in the future.' 'Keir Starmer has made it clear that only a political resolution can resolve this crisis in the long run, which is why we need a two-state solution,' a spokesperson said. Concurrently, Conservative councillors in Slough have issued an open letter advocating for 'an immediate ceasefire,' a stance that contradicts the government's official policy.

article_content: A revolutionary mobile home featuring a movable interior wall is poised to transform caravan holidays. This 'Concept Van', measuring merely 30ft by 13ft, boasts a cutting-edge design that allows the same area to serve multiple functions at different times. During the day, retracting the sliding bedroom wall unlocks an additional 60sqft, creating a spacious open-plan living area capable of accommodating a 10-seater dining table. Crafted by ABI, a holiday home manufacturer based in Beverley, East Yorkshire, the 'Concept Van' was unveiled at Hoburne Holiday Park in New Milton, Hampshire. At night, the wall can be repositioned to reveal a foldaway double bed. Concealed behind this wall are two single bunk beds that can be folded down once the wall is in place. With triple fixed bunk beds located at one end and a convertible sofa bed in the lounge, this mobile home, designed to accommodate six, can now comfortably house up to nine individuals. The only room with a fixed size is the bathroom. This innovation could enable holiday parks to accommodate more caravans by replacing larger, four-bedroom units. Currently a prototype, this ingenious caravan is predicted to redefine 'staycation' holidays. According to Richard Jones, a director at ABI, the aim was to create a caravan that uses space unconventionally. 'In a typical caravan, a bedroom remains a bedroom around the clock. However, for a significant portion of the day, this space remains unused.' He continued, 'By closing off the bedroom when it isn't needed, the space can be repurposed. We've employed technology similar to that used in large document storage systems to facilitate the movement of the central wall, allowing the bedroom space to be opened and closed as required.' Jones added, 'We've developed a remarkable van capable of accommodating nine holidaymakers for sleeping, dining, relaxation, and entertainment, all within a compact 30ft x 13ft footprint. Behind the main bedroom are two concealed single bunk beds that can be folded down. There are also three fixed bunk beds at one end of the caravan.' 'The design's core principle is to use the same space for various activities at different times,' explained Jones. 'To achieve this, we incorporated features such as pull-down beds, a triple bunk bed, a dining table that folds away when not in use, hidden kitchen worktops, a cinema screen that descends from the ceiling, and movable walls controlled by a button press.' 'We've received fantastic feedback and are eager to integrate these concepts into our future collections,' Jones concluded.

article_content: While they might make you feel cleaner than regular toilet paper, think twice before flushing wet wipes. Despite many celebrities endorsing their daily use, sewer utilities are struggling with clogged pipes and pumps. This growing problem has cost the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC) over $1 million to install machinery that shreds the wipes before they reach the pumps en route to treatment plants. Officials attribute a 35 percent increase in broken pumps and clogged sewer lines to wipes in recent years, according to The Washington Post. These wet wipes—often used for babies and thorough cleaning—also contribute to blockages that cause sewage to overflow into streams and back up into basements. Washington officials state that the problem is wet wipe products being marketed as flushable. 'Just because you can flush it doesn’t mean you should,' said I.J. Hudson, a spokesman for the WSSC, which manages sewage for 1.8 million residents in Montgomery and Prince George’s counties. DC Water officials report that over 500 man-hours were spent in the past 12 months removing stuck wipes and repairing broken equipment. In July, British sewerage workers discovered a 15-tonne mass of congealed fat and wet wipes, dubbed 'Fatberg,' that was the size of a bus. This toxic lump clogged 95 percent of a 2.4-meter diameter London sewer pipe and took three weeks for sewer workers to clear. Just a week prior, large masses of lard and baby wipes were found clogging Denver's sewers, including a giant grease ball under a resident's home causing drain backups. Workers found that the resident on Warren Ave had been regularly pouring grease down the sink, hardening into a lump and blocking the line. According to The Washington Post, wipe manufacturers claim they are trying to reduce wear and tear on sewer systems and septic tanks. The Association of the Nonwoven Fabrics Industry is creating a technical work group with utility officials to address concerns about how wipes are tested for flushability. This summer, the trade association released updated guidelines for wipe manufacturers, outlining seven tests a product should pass before being marketed as flushable. They also suggest more prominent 'Do Not Flush' logos on products that don't pass but are commonly used in bathrooms. Dave Rousse, president of the fabrics group, said consumers want durable baby wipes. 'We all agree the solution is to reduce the burden on wastewater treatment systems,' Rousse said. 'We agree we need to label products appropriately and educate the public to flush responsibly—to look for and obey disposal instructions.' The industry is booming, with consumer wipe sales predicted to grow by about 6 percent annually for the next five years, according to Rousse. Celebrities are endorsing daily wet wipe use, including actor Terrence Howard, who told Elle Magazine that women who don't use wipes are 'not completely clean.' Singer Bruno Mars says he always brings wet wipes on tour. 'If they’re using dry paper, they aren’t washing all of themselves. It’s just unclean. So if I go in a woman’s house and see the toilet paper there, I’ll explain this.' Hip hop singer and producer Will.i.am has expressed similar views to Elle Magazine. 'Here's proof on why people should have baby wipes. Get some chocolate, wipe it on a wooden floor, and then try to get it up with some dry towels. You're going to get chocolate in the cracks. That's why you gotta get them baby wipes.' The latest celebrity to advocate for wipes is singer Bruno Mars, who told TMZ.com that he always brings wipes and wine on tour. Actor Will Smith has also joined the baby wipes campaign, telling BBC’s Radio 1, 'I'm the type of person that it's important for me to share. When I experience something that's special and incredible, I like to share it with people. Anyone who's using dry toilet paper, you're really not doing yourself the true service.'
translated_content: Embora possam fazer você se sentir mais limpo do que o papel higiênico comum, pense duas vezes antes de jogar lenços umedecidos no vaso sanitário. Apesar de muitas celebridades endossarem o uso diário, as empresas de saneamento estão lutando contra tubulações e bombas entupidas. Este problema crescente custou à Comissão de Saneamento Suburbano de Washington (WSSC) mais de US$ 1 milhão para instalar máquinas que trituram os lenços antes que cheguem às bombas a caminho das estações de tratamento. As autoridades atribuem um aumento de 35% em bombas quebradas e linhas de esgoto entupidas aos lenços nos últimos anos, de acordo com o The Washington Post. Esses lenços umedecidos – frequentemente usados para bebês e para uma limpeza completa – também contribuem para bloqueios que causam o transbordamento de esgoto em riachos e o retorno para dentro de casas e prédios. As autoridades de Washington afirmam que o problema é que os produtos de lenços umedecidos estão sendo comercializados como 'descartáveis no vaso sanitário'. 'Só porque você pode jogar no vaso sanitário, não significa que deva', disse I.J. Hudson, porta-voz da WSSC, que administra o esgoto para 1,8 milhão de residentes nos condados de Montgomery e Prince George. Funcionários da DC Water relatam que mais de 500 horas de trabalho foram gastas nos últimos 12 meses removendo lenços presos e reparando equipamentos danificados. Em julho, trabalhadores de esgoto britânicos descobriram uma massa de 15 toneladas de gordura e lenços umedecidos, apelidada de 'Fatberg', que tinha o tamanho de um ônibus. Essa massa tóxica entupiu 95% de um cano de esgoto de Londres de 2,4 metros de diâmetro e levou três semanas para os trabalhadores do esgoto removerem. Apenas uma semana antes, grandes massas de gordura e lenços umedecidos para bebês foram encontradas entupindo os esgotos de Denver, incluindo uma bola de gordura gigante sob a casa de um morador causando entupimentos nos ralos. Os trabalhadores descobriram que o morador da Warren Ave estava despejando regularmente gordura na pia, que endureceu e bloqueou a tubulação. De acordo com o The Washington Post, os fabricantes de lenços afirmam que estão tentando reduzir o desgaste nos sistemas de esgoto e fossas sépticas. A Associação da Indústria de Tecidos Não Tecidos está criando um grupo de trabalho técnico com autoridades de serviços públicos para tratar das preocupações sobre como os lenços são testados para garantir que podem ser descartados no vaso sanitário com segurança. Neste verão, a associação comercial divulgou diretrizes atualizadas para os fabricantes de lenços, descrevendo sete testes que um produto deve passar antes de ser comercializado como 'descartável no vaso sanitário'. Eles também sugerem que os produtos que não atendem aos requisitos, mas são comumente usados em banheiros, exibam logotipos 'Não Jogue no Vaso Sanitário' de forma mais visível. Dave Rousse, presidente do grupo de tecidos, disse que os consumidores querem lenços umedecidos duráveis para bebês. 'Todos concordamos que a solução é reduzir a carga sobre os sistemas de tratamento de águas residuais', disse Rousse. 'Concordamos que precisamos rotular os produtos de forma adequada e educar o público a descartar os lenços de forma responsável – procurando e obedecendo às instruções de descarte.' A indústria está em expansão, com as vendas de lenços umedecidos para o consumidor com previsão de crescimento de cerca de 6% ao ano nos próximos cinco anos, de acordo com Rousse. Celebridades estão endossando o uso diário de lenços umedecidos, incluindo o ator Terrence Howard, que disse à revista Elle que as mulheres que não usam lenços umedecidos 'não estão completamente limpas'. O cantor Bruno Mars diz que sempre leva lenços umedecidos em turnê. 'Se elas estão usando papel seco, não estão se limpando completamente. É simplesmente anti-higiênico. Então, se eu entrar na casa de uma mulher e vir papel higiênico, vou explicar isso.' O cantor e produtor de hip hop Will.i.am expressou opiniões semelhantes à revista Elle. 'Aqui está a prova de por que as pessoas deveriam ter lenços umedecidos para bebês. Pegue um pouco de chocolate, passe em um piso de madeira e tente limpá-lo com toalhas secas. Você vai espalhar o chocolate nas rachaduras. É por isso que você precisa usar lenços umedecidos para bebês.' A celebridade mais recente a defender os lenços umedecidos é o cantor Bruno Mars, que disse ao TMZ.com que sempre leva lenços umedecidos e vinho em turnê. O ator Will Smith também aderiu à campanha de lenços umedecidos para bebês, dizendo à Rádio 1 da BBC: 'Para mim, é importante compartilhar. Quando experimento algo especial e incrível, gosto de compartilhar com as pessoas. Quem usa papel higiênico seco não está se cuidando adequadamente.'

article_content: Single mother Sanaa Derbas, 39, will face court next month, accused of defrauding elderly men of $2 million in a 'lonely hearts' scam, allegedly using the funds to support a lavish lifestyle. Derbas was arrested on Thursday at her home in Miller, in Sydney's west, and charged with fraud and money laundering, offences typically associated with international fraudsters. The prosecution alleges she targeted men in their 60s and 70s through online dating sites and newspaper ads. She reportedly used to own a cosmetics business called 'Provocative Nails'. Derbas, a mother of four whose children range from two to 16 years old, is scheduled to appear in court on June 25. She is believed to be the first person in Australia to face these charges in connection with a 'lonely hearts' scam. The prosecution claims that Derbas, who receives $1,500 every two weeks in welfare, used dating platforms such as Lavalife and Meeting Point to find older men. According to reports, she spent the allegedly ill-gotten gains on luxury vehicles, international vacations, designer handbags, and cosmetic surgery. She also allegedly demolished her Miller residence and constructed a new one. Following Derbas's arrest, a man named Gus, believed to be a relative, used a garden hose on reporters outside her mother's home, where Derbas's mother reportedly resides. A neighbor voiced support for Derbas, saying 'good on her, if they're that stupid', regarding the alleged defrauding of the elderly men. Another neighbor described Derbas as 'a lovely woman with lovely kids' who had rebuilt her home in recent years. A local resident stated that Derbas's family is of Lebanese descent and has lived in the area for many years, adding that Derbas 'fancies herself' and has had cosmetic procedures. Authorities claim one man gave Derbas $1.9 million, while others gave $190,000, $58,000, and $12,000, respectively; police suspect there may be more victims. Reportedly, three of the men had never met Derbas in person, and one, an interstate businessman, had a sexual relationship with her at his apartment. Detective Superintendent Arthur Katsogiannis of the NSW Fraud and Cybercrime Squad described Derbas as adept at manipulating older men, convincing them of a romantic relationship. NSW Police will allege that Derbas maintained five bank accounts and fabricated stories to persuade her victims to deposit money, such as claiming a relative in Egypt had died or her child required surgery in Melbourne. Police also allege she laundered money through the purchase and sale of vehicles at a loss. Detective Katsogiannis stated that this type of scam is more common overseas and believes this is the first instance of such charges in Australia. He commended the men for reporting the 'potentially very embarrassing' situation. Police have frozen over $1 million in assets and seized Derbas's cars. Derbas is currently on bail and is scheduled to appear at Liverpool Local Court on June 25.

article_content: A small dog proves that size isn't everything when it comes to causing mischief at a party. In Limassol, Cyprus, two men were setting up an outdoor entertaining area for a celebration when a playful puppy decided to start the festivities early. The black puppy grabbed the most colorful decoration it could find - a long line of bunting - and led the two men on a merry chase. The puppy darted under the tables and chairs, which had been arranged for the party, trying to evade capture. The men seemed careful not to injure the puppy or further damage the bunting as they pursued the dog. After about a minute, the puppy's game ended, and unfortunately for the men, the bunting was ruined. The puppy weaved through the tables and chairs, proving too elusive for the men until it decided it was finished playing.

article_content: After being struck by a shopping trolley at a Marks & Spencer, 60-year-old Michael Buckley has died, potentially leading to murder charges for the suspect. The incident, which occurred three days before Christmas, left Buckley with a broken hip and wrist. A 30-year-old woman was initially arrested for causing serious bodily harm. However, Buckley's health declined, and he passed away at Princess Royal University Hospital in Farnborough on Tuesday after suffering a heart attack. Buckley, described as frail, standing at approximately 5ft 4in and weighing around 8st, had significant hearing issues, requiring two hearing aids. He had retired from his gardening job at a cemetery due to his declining health. He lived alone after the death of his wife, Irene Christie, a former model and actress, two years prior, mourning her loss and caring for her macaw, Max, which once featured in the James Bond film 'For Your Eyes Only'. According to a neighbor, Buckley was a gentle man who was easily intimidated. The neighbor recounted hearing that the incident occurred when a woman demanded to pass him in the store, and despite Buckley's request for a moment, she allegedly pushed him. The neighbor further claimed that the woman returned to push him again, causing him to fall. He never recovered after being hospitalized. The incident took place in a crowded Marks & Spencer food hall in the Glades shopping centre in Bromley, south-east London, around 1pm during the pre-Christmas rush. Witnesses reported to the police that the woman intentionally shoved Buckley with her trolley, resulting in his fall. A staff member described the incident as a 'moment of madness,' stating that the woman seemed enraged by Buckley's slow movement. The staff member lamented the increasing impatience observed in shoppers. Another neighbor described Buckley as someone who appeared very fragile. A Metropolitan Police spokesperson confirmed the incident, stating that a 60-year-old man died after being struck by a shopping trolley on December 22 in Bromley, Kent. They added that police responded to a report of a man injured during an altercation at the shopping centre. The police statement indicated that Buckley was struck by a trolley pushed by a woman, causing him to fall and sustain injuries, including a broken hip and wrist, requiring hospital treatment. The police were informed on December 26 that Buckley had suffered further health complications and was in critical condition. A neighbor, who wished to remain anonymous, told News Shopper that she had known Buckley for 15 years and described him as a generous and well-liked man with a love for wildlife. She mentioned his annual trips to Arizona with his late wife, Irene, to film hummingbirds and his passion for Elvis Presley. However, she also noted his frailty and early retirement due to a knee injury. She reiterated his need for a hearing aid and his appearance of being older than his age, describing him as someone who looked like a strong breeze could knock him over. Staff at M & S suggested that the woman's attack was triggered by Buckley's failure to move quickly enough. This incident is part of a growing trend of 'trolley rage' in supermarkets. In a previous case, Hayley Cook, a pregnant 24-year-old mother, was sentenced to a year in jail for breaking a woman's pelvis outside a Tesco in Ramsgate after verbally abusing her and crashing her trolley into her. Another incident occurred in March of the same year at a Morrisons in Weymouth, Dorset, where an elderly man sustained a head wound after a fight broke out between shoppers over trolley bumping.

article_content: San Francisco's iconic Golden Gate Bridge is one step closer to having a much-debated suicide barrier after bridge officials on Friday approved a $76 million funding package for a net system designed to prevent suicides. The bridge district's board of directors unanimously approved funding for the steel suicide net, including $20 million from bridge toll revenue. Federal funds will cover most of the remaining cost, with the state pledging $7 million. Dan Barks, from Napa, who tearfully recalled losing his son, Donovan, to suicide on the bridge in 2008, said he was almost speechless after the vote. This undated artist's rendering, provided by Golden Gate Bridge authorities, depicts the proposed netting suicide barrier to be installed under the bridge. A sign is posted above a crisis counseling call box on the Golden Gate Bridge. 'A lot of people have done so much incredible work to accomplish this,' he said. After the vote, he embraced Sue Story from Rocklin, whose son Jacob jumped off the bridge in 2010. 'We did it, Dan! We did it! It's no longer the Bridge of Death,' she exclaimed. While some of the funding still requires approval, the bridge's board has taken its final step in adopting the net. 'The tragedy is that we cannot go back and save those who jumped. But with this vote, we honor their memory,' said board member Janet Reilly. 'We will save lives, and that is extraordinary.' The Golden Gate Bridge, with its sweeping views of the Pacific Ocean and San Francisco Bay, has been a destination for individuals seeking to end their lives. Roberta McLauglin photographed an exhibit of shoes commemorating people who jumped from the Golden Gate Bridge during the bridge's 75th anniversary on Sunday, May 27, 2012. Since opening in 1937, over 1,400 people have died by suicide, including a record 46 in 2013, officials reported. Officials have discussed a suicide barrier for decades. The bridge's board voted in 2008 to install a stainless steel net, rejecting options like raising the 4-foot railings and leaving the bridge unchanged. Two years later, they certified the final environmental impact report for the net, which would extend approximately 20 feet on each side. Officials assure it won't detract from the bridge's appearance. Funding remained a major obstacle until President Barack Obama signed a bill making safety barriers eligible for federal funds. House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi of California praised the board and Assemblyman Tom Ammiano, D-San Francisco, for their support. The Golden Gate Bridge district's board of directors unanimously approved a $76 million funding package to build the suicide barrier. 'The Golden Gate Bridge is a source of pride for San Francisco, but also a place of pain for many families,' Pelosi said. 'A suicide prevention barrier offers a second chance for individuals acting on impulsive thoughts. Together, we can ensure this landmark remains a companion for all San Franciscans, inspiring visitors for generations.' Most jumpers suffer severe internal injuries, broken bones, and skull fractures, often dying from internal bleeding or drowning. Kevin Hines, who miraculously survived his suicide attempt in 2000 at age 19, urged the board to 'not let one more family suffer eternal pain.' He later broke down after the vote, saying, 'I feel like a giant weight has been lifted. I feel a sense of hope. It's not over until that net is raised and no more people die.' Richard Gamboa of Sacramento, whose son, Kyle, was among the bridge suicides in 2013, said he's not done fighting. 'It's not over for me. I will keep urging them to get the barrier done. When I see that net, I will be at peace,' Gamboa said. John Brooks, whose 17-year-old daughter, Casey, jumped from the bridge in 2008, hopes for safety measures before the net's completion. 'I don't want to see more deaths,' Brooks said. 'That would be a cruel irony.' Board members and San Francisco supervisors David Campos and London Breed agreed the barrier should be built quickly. 'We need to build it as soon as we can,' Campos said. Bidding is expected to start next year, with completion anticipated in 2018.

John Brooks, cuja filha de 17 anos, Casey, saltou da ponte em 2008, espera que sejam tomadas medidas de segurança antes da conclusão da rede. “Não quero ver mais mortes”, disse Brooks. “Isso seria uma cruel ironia.” Os membros do conselho e os supervisores de São Francisco, David Campos e London Breed, concordaram que a barreira deve ser construída rapidamente. “Precisamos de construí-la o mais depressa possível”, disse Campos. Espera-se que as licitações comecem no próximo ano, prevendo-se a conclusão para 2018.

article_content: Macedonia's celebration of two decades of independence from the former Yugoslavia was set against the backdrop of a capital dramatically reshaped in just two years. The city center of Skopje now boasts nearly twenty newly constructed buildings, complemented by a similar number of statues, fountains, and monuments. These changes are part of the 'Skopje 2014' initiative, which aims to reconstruct a city that had many landmarks destroyed in the 1963 earthquake. A central feature, unveiled for the anniversary celebrations on September 8, was a 22-meter-tall statue called 'Warrior on a Horse'. Though widely believed to represent Alexander the Great, it hasn't been officially named so due to a longstanding disagreement with Greece, where Alexander is a national icon. Other recent additions include the Museum of Macedonian Struggle (opened on Independence Day), a triumphal arch, and new buildings for the foreign ministry, constitutional court, national theater, and archaeological museum. While the official price tag for the project is 80 million euros, the online publication Balkan Insight suggests that the actual cost could climb as high as 500 million euros. The Skopje 2014 project has sparked debate among Macedonians. Some argue that a nation grappling with over 30% unemployment, according to U.N. figures, shouldn't allocate so much to construction. Goran Atanasovski, who manages the independent travel website travel2macedonia.com.mk, noted that the project divides the populace, with supporters and detractors on opposite sides. He emphasized the controversy stems mainly from Macedonia's economic challenges. However, Zoran Nikolovski, the head of government tourism, asserted that Skopje has been transformed in the past two years and will continue to evolve with even more new structures by 2014. He highlighted the country's ongoing development of infrastructure and accommodation, despite the global economic downturn, including new airports, roads, and hotels. Nikolovski acknowledged initial public skepticism but believes people now recognize the beauty it brings to Skopje for residents and visitors alike. Beyond practical considerations, some have questioned the aesthetic of the classical-style buildings and bronze sculptures. One anonymous Macedonian resident mentioned avoiding the city center due to its transformation into a 'theme park' filled with bronze statues, which they feel is an attempt to forge a national identity. They expressed a preference for modern, urban designs suitable for the 21st century rather than constructing a triumphal arch. Regardless of personal opinions, the Skopje 2014 project and other infrastructure investments seem to be drawing more international tourists to Macedonia. Nikolovski reported a 25% increase in foreign visitors during the first seven months of the year compared to the same period last year. Atanasovski observed that this was the first season he witnessed numerous foreign tourist groups with guides in both the downtown area and the Old Bazaar, regardless of whether Skopje 2014 was the cause. Skopje has even surpassed Ohrid, a leading Macedonian tourist destination, in attracting tourists this year. Official government figures show a consistent rise in foreign tourist arrivals, from 99,000 in 2001 to nearly 262,000 last year. While most visitors are from neighboring countries, there has been a growing influx from countries farther away such as Austria, Germany, Russia, Poland, Italy, and Turkey. Nikolovski explained that while Macedonia lacks a coastline for mass market tourism, it compensates with stunning lakes, mountains, and a rich culture and history. The country is also actively growing its gambling tourism sector, featuring several casino hotels. To further stimulate tourism, the government has implemented policies like reducing sales tax on hotels and catering services from 18% to 5% and offering subsidies to attract tour groups from specific nations. Atanasovski noted that previously, tour operators would include Macedonia as part of broader Balkan tours with brief one-day stays. However, since last year, the number of nights tourists spend in Macedonia has increased. Despite the financial investments in significant projects and infrastructure, national pride received an unexpected boost from the national basketball team's surprising advancement to the European championship semi-finals. Atanasovski remarked that he had never seen Macedonians so joyful and proud. He described flags displayed everywhere, symbolizing the nation's ability to replace their economic woes with smiles and happiness.

Atanasovski observou que, anteriormente, os operadores turísticos incluíam a Macedónia como parte de passeios mais amplos pelos Balcãs, com breves estadias de um dia. In Los Angeles, California, a federal judge sentenced Michael David Barrett, a 49-year-old Illinois man, to two and a half years in prison on Monday for secretly taping ESPN sports reporter Erin Andrews in the nude. The surreptitious recording occurred through a peephole in a hotel room, and the video was subsequently posted online. Barrett pleaded guilty to a federal stalking charge in December after prosecutors accused him of altering hotel peepholes to record Andrews while she was undressed.

According to a plea agreement, both prosecutors and Barrett had consented to a 27-month prison sentence. However, Andrews, referring to him as a sexual predator, advocated in court for the maximum sentence allowed by law, as reported by CNN affiliate KTLA. 'I would have liked a longer sentence, but I understand that the judge did the best he could within the established legal parameters,' Andrews told reporters outside the courthouse following the sentencing. 'I am relieved that he will be unable to harm anyone that he could harm for the next 30 months.'

Court documents revealed that Barrett, an insurance company employee from Westmont, Illinois, posted approximately 10 videos of Andrews online. These documents also indicated that Barrett had posted videos of another 16 victims, who remain unidentified, on the Internet.

Barrett, who has been free on bail, is scheduled to report to prison on May 3, according to Tom Mrozek, a spokesman for the U.S. attorney's office in Los Angeles. In a statement released through his attorney when the plea agreement was announced, Barrett conveyed his 'deep regret' to Andrews 'for his conduct that caused her so much pain.'

Authorities suspect that the majority of the videos were recorded at a hotel in Nashville, Tennessee, in September 2008. The peephole into Andrews' room had been tampered with using a hacksaw, and the footage appeared to have been captured with a cell phone camera, according to the charges against Barrett. Andrews travels nationwide covering college football games for ESPN.

According to charges filed against Barrett in October, Andrews stated that she became aware of the videos in July and that their online posting caused her significant distress, anxiety, and sleep disturbances. Barrett initially came under investigation after attempting to sell the videos to the celebrity gossip site TMZ in January 2009. TMZ declined to purchase the images but assisted the investigation by providing information to Andrews' attorneys, authorities confirmed. Both TMZ and CNN are subsidiaries of Time Warner Inc. CNN's Lynn Lamanivong contributed to this report.

article_content: A tragic tale from 1915 reveals a suicide pact between a soldier and his wife, driven by their fear of the First World War's horrors. The discovery was made in archive records. Shadrach Critchley, age 35, and his wife Annie, age 45, were found deceased next to each other on a mattress in their Leigh, Greater Manchester home on May 24, 1915. This occurred shortly after Shadrach was conscripted into the Cheshire Regiment. Historical newspaper clippings indicate that the couple left handwritten notes, expressing their mutual desire 'never to be parted'. Volunteer historian Susan Berry, 50, unearthed this poignant story during her genealogical research. According to Ms. Berry, many associate World War One with battlefield deaths, but Shadrach and Annie's deaths highlight the war's wider impact. 'The story made me think about what people must have been going through emotionally when the men went off to war.' Born in 1881, Shadrach Critchley grew up in Leigh, working as a coal miner like his father, Thomas. He married Annie Heaton in 1906. The 1911 census suggests they lived in Westleigh, Greater Manchester, and had no children. Local newspapers documented Shadrach Critchley's recruitment into the Army in April 1915. He was stationed in Birkenhead and was granted three days of leave, returning home on May 22. His fellow soldier Richard Adamson recalled Shadrach expressing regret about enlisting while at the Fleece Inn the night before returning to his regiment. Adamson attempted to reassure him. The next evening, Adamson found Shadrach and Annie deceased on a mattress in their kitchen after forcing open the door. The inquest revealed the couple's notes expressing their desire to remain together always. They were buried together in St Paul’s churchyard in Westleigh. The jury delivered a verdict of temporary insanity. Shadrach Critchley received posthumous recognition on the Brookwood Memorial, which lists approximately 500 men who died on British soil. Erected in 2004, the memorial is located in Surrey, adjacent to a large cemetery where over 1,500 Commonwealth servicemen who died in the UK from their wounds are buried, nearly 90 years after Shadrach’s death. Hannah Turner, from Leigh Local Studies, stated, 'It’s a very sad story and one we had never come across before. It shows that the deaths during the war didn’t just happen on the battlefield.'

article_content: If you enjoy streaming films and sports, you might want to avoid Alaska, as it has the slowest internet connection in the United States. A Washington Post article featured a map from Broadview detailing average broadband speeds across the US, with Virginia leading at 13.7 megabits per second. Many northeastern states also show strong connectivity. Compared globally, the U.S. trails behind 11 other nations, including South Korea, Israel, and Romania, in terms of internet speed. Examining the data state by state reveals a range of average internet speeds, with faster connections indicated by green and slower ones by red. Virginia, Delaware, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, D.C., Washington, New Hampshire, Utah, Michigan and Connecticut are among the states with the fastest internet speeds. Ashburn, Virginia, often referred to as 'the bullseye of America's Internet' by Gizmodo, likely contributes to Virginia's leading broadband performance. The presence of major network hubs like Verizon and Facebook in this area results in some of the quickest connection speeds available. Washington, home to the tech giant Amazon, similarly demonstrates notably higher speeds than many other states. Akamai, a web hosting service based in Massachusetts that supports sites like Best Buy and FOX Sports, provided the raw data for the map in June. Akamai's quarterly report on global internet conditions includes information on connection speeds and web security. While states with slower speeds are marked in red and faster states in green, there's good news overall: internet speeds are increasing almost everywhere. Alaska saw a 33% improvement year-over-year, reaching 7 Mbps. Kansas experienced the most dramatic improvement, with speeds increasing by 91% to 8.6 Mbps.

article_content: A former British police officer, Chris Devereux, who retired to the Cayman Islands after 30 years on the force, has died in a scuba diving accident. Chris Devereux, 54, moved abroad to help lead an anti-crime drive with the Royal Cayman Islands Police Service. The experienced detective, who had previously served with Merseyside Police, died after experiencing difficulties while diving off-duty at a popular spot near an underwater mermaid sculpture off Sunset House, near George Town, the capital. The former British police officer died after encountering difficulties while diving at a popular spot off Sunset House, near George Town, the capital. He was swimming near an underwater mermaid sculpture. The detective was pronounced dead on arrival at a nearby hospital after a colleague brought him to the surface. Mr. Devereux moved to the Caribbean island in May of this year. A police spokesman on the island, which is also a well-known financial tax haven, said: 'The officer had been shore diving with a colleague when he experienced difficulty and lost consciousness. 'His colleague brought him to the surface. Staff from Sunset House immediately assisted, brought him to shore, and performed CPR.' 'When the ambulance crew arrived, they continued CPR while conveying the officer to the Cayman Islands Hospital in George Town.' 'However, despite the efforts of the dive staff and the paramedics, he was pronounced dead on arrival.' 'A family liaison officer has been appointed by the RCIPS, and efforts are being made to contact his next of kin.' 'He was a very dedicated officer and was involved in many investigations,' said RCIPS Superintendent Kurt Walton. The veteran officer was assigned to the RCIPS Drugs and Serious Crime Task Force as a detective constable. Cayman Islands is where Mr. Devereux moved to help lead an anti-crime drive. He was one of several UK officers who came to work in Cayman after the island police force received an additional £3 million in government funding to bolster its ranks following a gang-related killing spree in September 2011. Mr. Devereux’s former boss and colleague, Merseyside Chief Constable Jon Murphy, praised his former officer. 'It was with sadness that I heard about the death of former Merseyside Police Detective Constable Chris Devereux in the Cayman Islands yesterday.' 'Having served with him as a cadet and then at several points during his career, I would describe him as a hard-working and likeable man, as well as an outstanding police officer dedicated to serving the people of Merseyside for 30 years.' 'As an experienced detective, he was involved in a number of complex investigations and was a valued member of Merseyside Police. 'He will be sadly missed.’ Police Commissioner David Baines also said in a statement: ‘Although Chris had only been with the RCIPS for a matter of months, he had quickly become an integral part of the Drugs and Serious Crime Task Force. ‘He was both well-liked and respected by colleagues. He will be remembered as a hard-working and committed officer who played a significant role in some of our most recent investigations. article_content: North Korea has announced that American tourist Kenneth Bae will soon face trial on charges of attempting to subvert the government. This declaration comes after weeks of heightened tensions and strong rhetoric directed towards both the United States and South Korea. Bae, identified by North Korean state media as Pae Jun Ho, is a tour operator of Korean heritage. He was taken into custody upon his arrival on November 3 with a tour group in Rason, a special economic zone situated near the borders of China and Russia. He marks the sixth American to be detained in North Korea since 2009. Previously, detained Americans were either deported or freed following significant diplomatic interventions, some of which involved former Presidents Bill Clinton and Jimmy Carter. Analysts suggest that North Korea is likely to impose a severe penalty on Bae, intending to utilize him as leverage in potential negotiations with the United States. In a brief statement, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported, 'The preliminary inquiry into the crimes committed by American citizen Pae Jun Ho has concluded. During the investigation, he confessed to committing acts aimed at overthrowing the DPRK with hostile intent. The evidence confirmed his crimes.' Sources familiar with Bae, including friends and South Korean activists focusing on North Korean affairs, describe him as a Christian missionary operating from a Chinese border town. He reportedly made frequent trips into North Korea to provide aid to orphans. It remains unclear whether he engaged in evangelistic activities while in North Korea. Although North Korea officially guarantees religious freedom, the government actively suppresses Christianity, viewing it as a Western-influenced threat. Defectors have reported that distributing Bibles or holding clandestine prayer services can result in imprisonment in labor camps or even execution.

article_content: America's institutions have been shaken by a series of political corruption scandals. In recent times, several elected officials have been caught using their public roles to enrich themselves, their families, or allies. For example, this week, U.S. Rep. George Santos ended his re-election campaign after a House ethics report indicated he used campaign money for personal purposes. U.S. Sen. Bob Menendez is currently facing a second bribery charge. (Both deny these allegations). Additionally, former Ohio House Speaker Larry Householder was found guilty in a $60 million bribery plot. The USC Sol Price School of Public Policy emphasizes ethics and selfless service to its students. Therefore, we consulted some of their experts to find out what causes these scandals and what actions can reduce corruption, which harms government trust. 'If you're already distrustful of the government, these abuses worsen the situation,' said LaVonna B. Lewis, USC Price School Professor. 'You shouldn't judge an entire institution based on a few people's actions, but unfortunately, those actions often receive the most attention.' Individual Morality vs. the System Frank V. Zerunyan, Professor at the USC Price School, notes that corruption is an inherent human issue. Many officials let their power corrupt them, justifying their actions. 'We're all human,' said Zerunyan, a council member of Rolling Hills Estates, Calif. 'I tell my students that without discipline and a strong ethical compass, human weaknesses can lead to ethical breaches.' Mindy Romero, Assistant Professor at USC Price School, explained that the U.S. political system places pressure even on ethical politicians. Success requires balancing constituent needs with the demands of political leaders, donors, and advocacy groups, which are vital for career advancement. This balance can cause officials to vote against their constituents' wishes. 'People prioritize their own survival,' Romero said. 'The system often forces elected officials to compromise their beliefs and the best interests of their voters.' Is there more corruption now? The U.S. is one of the world's least corrupt countries, ranking 24th out of 180, according to Transparency International. USC Price School experts also noted that it's not clear whether there is more corruption or just more awareness of it. (For comparison, Denmark is the least corrupt and second happiest country). Experts say that technology is a factor in uncovering more scandals, providing more digital evidence. For example, Menendez's online search history reportedly showed searches for the value of gold bars. Lewis notes that these scandals can damage public trust. She believes that recognizing public officials who consistently act in the public interest is vital. 'We rarely celebrate those who have acted ethically for decades,' Lewis said. What solutions exist? 'We need to remove financial incentives from politics,' Romero added. 'People pursue political careers for power and financial gain, and money is heavily involved in politics.' Zerunyan teaches his students ethics, the importance of public service, and their future roles as public representatives. 'We teach them that public service is selfless. If you seek personal gain, don't enter public service, or you'll dishonor yourself and your family,' Zerunyan said.

article_content: One school playing field has been sold off approximately every two weeks since the London 2012 Olympics, according to new figures. Ministers have approved 26 sales since pledging to leverage the games to create a lasting sporting legacy for children. The Coalition, formed in May 2010, promised to ‘seek to protect school playing fields’. Official figures indicate that 57 disposals of school fields have been authorized since 2010, despite initial promises to the contrary. The pace of these sell-offs accelerated during the year of the Olympics. The Government maintains that pitches approved for disposal were often unused or surplus to the schools’ requirements. It states that proceeds from these disposals are reinvested in either sporting or educational facilities. The Sport and Recreation Alliance, representing over 300 sporting organizations, argues that access to adequate facilities is a ‘pre-requisite to tackling the growing crisis of inactivity among young people’. The figures reveal that 14 sell-offs were permitted in the Coalition's first year and 12 between May 2011 and April 2012. The following year, this number rose to 19, and in the six months between May 2013 and October 2013 – the most recent period for which data is available – 12 had already been approved. These sites are frequently sold to housing developers. Despite pledges, the spectacle and pageantry of the 2012 London Olympics has not prevented the sale of school fields nationwide. In six instances, the Government overruled its own advisory body to push through sales. During the August 2012 Olympics, as the country celebrated Team GB’s achievements, David Cameron pledged to harness the games' inspiration to ‘get children playing sport more regularly’, particularly competitive sport. In that year, Education Secretary Michael Gove apologized after it was revealed that the number of sell-offs under the Coalition was higher than initially admitted. He also faced criticism for rejecting the advice of the School Playing Fields Advisory Panel – an independent expert committee legally mandated to provide recommendations on each sale application. A new report details disposals since May 2010 and the rationale behind each. In 38 cases, schools closed or merged with others. In seven, the land was leased to other organizations, with pupils retaining access during school hours. In 12 cases, the land in question was ‘small sections of playing field…that either isn’t used by the school for sport or is not needed due to other facilities in place’. The Department for Education stated: ‘No open school has disposed of its entire playing field, and in every case all of the money made by the local authority or school from the sale will be invested in local sports or education facilities. ‘Every school must, by law, have access to enough playing field space to allow for its sports and curriculum needs to be met.’ The Department also noted that the number of disposals is decreasing. An average of 28 applications per year were approved under the last Labour government, compared to an average of 16 annually under the Coalition. Sallie Barker, interim chief executive at the Sport and Recreation Alliance, expressed particular concern regarding potential land sell-offs at newly-built academies and free schools. ‘There is no room for complacency, and access to decent facilities is a pre-requisite to tackling the growing crisis of inactivity among young people.’

A Sport and Recreation Alliance, representando mais de 300 organizações desportivas, argumenta que o acesso a instalações adequadas é um 'pré-requisito para enfrentar a crescente crise de inatividade entre os jovens'. Os números revelam que 14 vendas foram permitidas no primeiro ano da Coligação e 12 entre maio de 2011 e abril de 2012. No ano seguinte, este número subiu para 19 e, nos seis meses entre maio de 2013 e outubro de 2013 – o período mais recente para o qual os dados estão disponíveis – 12 já tinham sido aprovadas. Estes locais são frequentemente vendidos a promotores imobiliários. Apesar das promessas, o espetáculo e a pompa das Olimpíadas de Londres de 2012 não impediram a venda de campos escolares em todo o país. Em seis casos, o Governo anulou o seu próprio órgão consultivo para forçar as vendas. Durante as Olimpíadas de agosto de 2012, enquanto o país celebrava as conquistas do Team GB, David Cameron prometeu aproveitar a inspiração dos jogos para 'fazer com que as crianças pratiquem desporto com mais regularidade', principalmente desportos competitivos. Naquele ano, o Secretário de Educação Michael Gove pediu desculpa depois de ter sido revelado que o número de vendas sob a Coligação era maior do que o inicialmente admitido. Ele também foi criticado por rejeitar o conselho do Painel Consultivo de Campos de Jogos Escolares – um comité independente de especialistas legalmente obrigado a fornecer recomendações sobre cada pedido de venda. Um novo relatório detalha as alienações desde maio de 2010 e a justificação por trás de cada uma. Em 38 casos, as escolas fecharam ou fundiram-se com outras. Em sete, o terreno foi arrendado a outras organizações, com os alunos a manter o acesso durante o horário escolar. Em 12 casos, o terreno em questão era 'pequenas secções do campo de jogos... que não são usadas pela escola para desporto ou não são necessárias devido a outras instalações existentes'. O Departamento de Educação afirmou: 'Nenhuma escola aberta alienou todo o seu campo de jogos e, em todos os casos, todo o dinheiro arrecadado pela autoridade local ou pela escola com a venda será investido em instalações desportivas ou educacionais locais. 'Todas as escolas devem, por lei, ter acesso a espaço suficiente no campo de jogos para permitir que as suas necessidades desportivas e curriculares sejam atendidas.' O Departamento também observou que o número de alienações está a diminuir. Uma média de 28 pedidos por ano foram aprovados sob o último governo trabalhista, em comparação com uma média de 16 anualmente sob a Coligação. Sallie Barker, diretora executiva interina da Sport and Recreation Alliance, expressou particular preocupação com relação às potenciais vendas de terrenos em academias e escolas gratuitas recém-construídas. 'Não há espaço para complacência e o acesso a instalações decentes é um pré-requisito para enfrentar a crescente crise de inatividade entre os jovens.'
