article_content: If your dinner parties frequently go awry, the plates might be to blame, not just the cooking. Studies suggest that crockery, cutlery, and music are as important to the enjoyment of a meal as the food itself. Volunteers who ate a strawberry dessert from a white plate perceived it as 10 percent sweeter compared to those who ate the same dessert from a black plate. The study also indicated that popcorn tastes less salty when served in a red container than in a blue one. Professor Charles Spence, an Oxford University psychologist who conducted the experiments, also discovered that food tasted better when consumed with heavier cutlery and crockery. He explained, 'For years, we have focused on the taste, color, and sound of the food. While this is crucial, we are now seeing the emergence of an area that has been largely overlooked: everything else that accompanies food.' 'We never eat food in isolation; it is always served with cutlery, on a plate, on a table. Changing these elements can significantly influence the experience.' Professor Spence's experiments demonstrate that simple factors like plate color or spoon weight can make a considerable difference. Research shows that strawberry desserts taste 10 percent sweeter on a white plate than on a black one. The experiments showed that popcorn tastes saltier when eaten from a blue bowl compared to a red one. Professor Spence, who has collaborated with top chefs like Heston Blumenthal, suggests that color contrast may contribute to this phenomenon. Habit might also play a role. Salty crisps are commonly packaged in blue bags, which might explain why popcorn tasted saltier when eaten from a blue bowl. Weight is also significant, with heavier cutlery and crockery enhancing the taste of food. Professor Spence stated, 'Heavier spoons and bowls make food taste better.' This may be because we associate weight with value. Professor Spence advises those planning a dinner party to dedicate as much thought to the table setting as to the food itself. He suggests that when considering everything from plate color to cutlery weight, at least half of the enjoyment of a meal may stem from how it is served rather than how it tastes. Additional ideas include matching the background music to the wine. Research from the US and UK indicates that Cabernet Sauvignon is more enjoyable when paired with The Doors’ classic 'People are Strange'. The high pitch and fast tempo of Blondie’s 'Atomic' are said to enhance the taste of Chablis and Chardonnay, while Enya’s 'Orinoco Flow' may help Syrah go down more smoothly. Professor Spence has also shown that Pavarotti’s rendition of 'Nessun Dorma' accentuates the tanginess of dark chocolate and coffee-flavored desserts.

article_content: Three Marines are facing court martial proceedings for allegedly hazing a fellow Marine, Lance Cpl. Harry Lew, who subsequently committed suicide in Afghanistan in April. The case gained national prominence after Rep. Judy Chu of California, Lew's aunt, discussed it before a congressional committee in September. According to a Marine statement released Thursday, Brig. Gen. Frederick Padilla, commanding general of the 3rd Marine Division, has referred charges against Sgt. Benjamin E. Johns, Lance Cpl. Jacob D. Jacoby, and Lance Cpl. Carlos Orozco III to a general court martial. These three Marines reportedly berated and assaulted Lance Cpl. Lew for falling asleep while on watch shortly after his arrival in Afghanistan, as stated by Chu and a Marine investigation reported by the Marine Corps Times. Lew died by suicide, shooting himself not long after the alleged hazing. "Harry's death was a devastating tragedy that could have been avoided," Chu said in a statement released by her office on Thursday. "The Marine Corps' decision to bring these three Marines before a jury of their peers provides solace to the family and demonstrates the military justice system in action." During her September testimony before the House Armed Services Committee, Chu stated that her nephew's sergeant instructed other Marines in the unit to "teach" the 21-year-old newcomer after he was discovered asleep on watch. "Lance Corporal Lew was subjected to beatings, verbal abuse, and forced rigorous exercises," she said at the time. "He was forced to perform push-ups and leg lifts while wearing full body armor, and sand was poured into his mouth. He was made to dig a hole for hours. He was kicked, punched, and stomped on. This abuse continued until 3:20 a.m." Chu added that minutes later, Lew "climbed into the foxhole he had just dug, shot himself, and committed suicide." A military investigation report obtained by the Marine Corps Times indicated that Lew killed himself with a two- or three-round burst from an M249 Squad Automatic Weapon in the early hours of April 3. The Marine Corps Times reported that a message found on Lew's arm, believed to be a suicide note, read: "May hate me now, but in the long run this was the right choice. I'm sorry my mom deserves the truth." The incident at Patrol Base Gowragi, in the Nawa district, began when Lew failed to respond to radio calls late on the night of April 2, the report stated. According to the Marine Corps Times, a sergeant who found him sleeping told others that "peers should correct peers." The report further detailed how two lance corporals, whose names were redacted, berated Lew and forced him to do exercises in body armor for hours, with one of them occasionally stomping on Lew's legs. The report also stated that one Marine kicked and punched Lew until another Marine intervened. Less than an hour later, Lew took his own life. "At 0343 on 3 April 2011, while crouching in the fighting position he had just dug, LCpl Lew leaned over his M249 Squad Automatic Weapon, pointed the muzzle into his mouth, pulled the trigger, and intentionally killed himself," the report stated, according to the Marine Corps Times. CNN's Larry Shaughnessy contributed to this report.

article_content: Tim Yeo, a high-ranking Conservative MP, has been exonerated from claims that he exploited his position to assist green energy firms in lobbying government officials. A probe by the parliamentary standards committee, a body that oversees ethical conduct, concluded that Mr. Yeo's actions, which were brought to light through a newspaper investigation, did not contravene any established regulations. Mr. Yeo had previously stepped down from his role as chair of the Commons Energy and Climate Change Committee back in June. Undercover reporters, pretending to represent a fictitious solar power company, approached Mr. Yeo with an offer of a consultancy contract worth £7,000 per day. He was recorded stating that he could arrange introductions to key individuals, including government ministers, leveraging his extensive network. Rules within the House of Commons explicitly forbid MPs from acting as paid lobbyists advocating for specific interests before ministers. Mr. Yeo was also questioned about his committee's interactions with John Smith, the managing director of GB Railfreight. Having declared his financial interest as a paid director and shareholder of Eurotunnel, the parent company of GB Railfreight, Mr. Yeo refrained from asking Mr. Smith any questions during the committee meeting. However, he later told the reporters that he had advised Mr. Smith on what to say. The standards committee criticized the methods used by the journalists, citing 'deception, distortion, and selective quoting'. They stated that while media investigations can play a role in upholding standards of public conduct, Mr. Yeo had not violated any rules, and the primary misrepresentation came from the journalists themselves. Standards commissioner Kathryn Hudson found no proof that Mr. Yeo had coached his business associate but advised him to consider more carefully the potential implications of his statements. She did suggest a broader inquiry into whether committee chairmen should face restrictions on their outside interests, noting the potential for conflicts of interest despite the benefits these roles can bring to their work. Mr. Yeo emphasized that he could not act as a 'public advocate' and that ministers would independently assess the product's merits. Mr. Yeo, who previously served as an environment minister, is tasked with scrutinizing the energy policies of ministers and companies. However, he has faced criticism for earning £400,000 over the past three years from commercial ventures, largely related to green energy. He has also disagreed with George Osborne regarding proposed cuts to green taxes. In a statement, Mr. Yeo welcomed the report, stating that the Parliamentary Standards Commissioner had confirmed that he did not breach House rules following a comprehensive investigation. This included a thorough review of the full video recording provided to the commissioner by the Sunday Times. He emphasized that the commissioner's findings, as well as the committee's, were based on his actual statements rather than the newspaper's reported version.

Enfatizou que as conclusões do comissário, bem como as do comitê, foram baseadas em suas declarações reais, e não na versão noticiada pelo jornal.

article_content: By Katy Winter. When it comes to our love lives, it seems that we are a superstitious nation at heart. Research has revealed that one in 10 Britons admits to owning a set of 'lucky underwear', with most men and women keeping hold of their blessed briefs for four years, and 16 per cent of people keeping their special pants for over a decade. According to a study by Mecca Bingo, lucky underwear has led to over a third of Brits having sex (35 per cent), and almost a quarter (19 per cent) claim to have won money while wearing their trusted pants. Some Brits were fortunate enough to be proposed to (13 per cent), and one in four men (27 per cent) say they have witnessed their sports team win as a result of wearing their special shorts. TOWIE star Ferne McCann has been posing in specially created 'lucky pants' in her local bingo hall in Dagenham to promote the initiative. To celebrate this research, Mecca Bingo has created a pair of shorts for men and briefs for women, available on a first-come, first-served basis for a suggested charity donation of £2. Fresh from her stint on the TOWIE Marbella special, reality star Ferne McCann has been modeling the women's lucky pants: black and white briefs featuring tiny red hearts. Posing in her local bingo hall in a pair of heels and a cropped T-shirt, Ferne said: 'It’s fascinating to hear that so many people have lucky underwear.' 'I’ve never owned a pair of lucky undies, so I’m thrilled to finally have a set of my own - I can’t wait to test them out!' The survey by Mecca Bingo revealed that most women's lucky knickers are a classic brief style in black or white. When asked why they believe their undies are lucky, almost half the nation said it was because they felt comfortable in them. But for one third of Brits, it is simply because something positive had happened while wearing them. Celebrities such as Katy Perry also seem to be following the trend. According to the New York Daily News, the ‘ROAR’ singer bought President Obama his own pair of lucky underwear at a political rally in London just before he won the 2012 election. ITV presenter Ant McPartlin claims he hasn’t made a live appearance in 25 years without donning his lucky white underwear. Like Ant, most men aren’t too daring when it comes to what’s down under, with almost 50 per cent wearing boxers in either traditional black (25 per cent) or blue (18 per cent). When it comes to patterns, vertical stripes came out on top, followed by horizontal stripes and checkered squares. Black (23 per cent), red (21 per cent), and white (20 per cent) were the most popular colours amongst the ladies in a ‘classic style’ brief, with almost a quarter (24 per cent) of women slipping them on to increase their chances of getting lucky. Red hearts came out on top as the most popular ‘lucky’ pattern with 12 per cent of the vote, followed by flowers (10 per cent), polka dots (9 per cent), and stars (8 per cent). Donna Dawson, a psychologist specializing in Personality and Behaviour, explains: 'Lucky undies become ‘lucky’ because their owners connect wearing them to positive events and continue to be ‘lucky’ because their owners believe in their power.' 'Wearing the lucky pair becomes a self-fulfilling prophecy, as they make people feel more comfortable, relaxed, and confident, which in turn makes them better able to recognise and respond to positive opportunities that come along.' 'Lucky items such as underwear give people a sense of power and control over their environment, which is really what good luck is all about.' Katy Perry apparently bought President Obama his own pair of lucky underwear at a rally in London just before he won the 2012 election. A spokesman for Mecca Bingo explains: 'Our customers have all kinds of lucky rituals from jewelry to cuddly toys.' 'We know that lucky undies are also a popular choice, so we thought why not find out what the nation’s luckiest pair would look like, create them, and make them available to our customers?' The money raised will go to the Carers Trust, which Mecca Bingo supports nationwide. For those nowhere near the Essex region, a limited number will also be available via Mecca Bingo’s social media channels, where fans are able to try their luck to win a pair.

article_content: A student from Langley School, a boarding institution costing £24,000 annually, received a prison sentence for stabbing another student following a disagreement about soy sauce. Minheng He, an 18-year-old boarder, assaulted the other student at Langley School in Loddon, Norfolk, last October. The incident led to significant injuries on the victim's elbow and shoulder, causing a loss of two pints of blood. He was sentenced at Norwich Crown Court after confessing to wounding with intent. Judge Nicholas Coleman gave him a four-year sentence in a young offenders' institute. The judge stated that He executed a 'serious pre-meditated' assault on an 'innocent unarmed victim,' resulting in 'appalling' injuries. He armed himself with a knife in what the judge described as a planned revenge attack. Prosecutor Andrew Shaw noted the victim was preparing a meal with another student around 7:30 pm on October 7 when He approached requesting soy sauce, which was denied. An argument ensued, and the victim jokingly asked He how much he intended to pay for it, which He did not appreciate. Witnesses reported He telling the victim to 'wait where he was' before leaving. Later that night, around 10:30 pm, He entered the victim's room as he was doing homework and attacked him. The victim tried to defend himself and was stabbed in the arm and shoulder. He was later seen agitated, holding a bloody knife, and reportedly said 'I don't care any more.' The prosecution emphasized the time lapse between the initial argument and the stabbing, highlighting the premeditated nature of the attack. School staff responded, and He told a teacher that he acted due to an insult against his mother. Defense attorney Jonathan Goodman argued for leniency, citing He's guilty plea and previous good character. He mentioned He's isolation, his mother's cancer diagnosis, and his remorse for his actions. Dominic Findlay, the headteacher of Langley School, expressed relief that the matter was resolved and that a guilty plea was entered.

article_content: In Cebu, Philippines, inmates at a prison, including convicted murderers, rapists, and drug dealers, honored Michael Jackson on Saturday with a rendition of their popular YouTube dance performance of 'Thriller'. The prisoners' version of Jackson's 1980s hit, performed at the Cebu Detention and Rehabilitation Center in the central Philippines, has received over 24 million views since prison supervisor Byron Garcia uploaded it to YouTube in 2007. The prison has since shared other dance videos online, featuring performances to songs such as Van Halen's 'Jump,' Queen's 'Radio Ga Ga,' and Phil Oakey and Giorgio Moroder's 'Together in Electric Dreams'. Jackson, the 'King of Pop,' passed away in Los Angeles on Thursday, shortly before his scheduled comeback concerts in London, England. Upon hearing the news, Garcia, a fan of the 50-year-old singer, organized a free tribute performance in the prison courtyard for local residents. Dancing was introduced at the prison in 2007 as a means of rehabilitating inmates at a facility that had been plagued by gang violence. Participation in dance is mandatory for all able-bodied prisoners. Refusal results in the loss of privileges, primarily conjugal visits. Garcia stated that dancing occupies up to five hours daily but refuted claims of abusing prisoners' rights by forcing them to dance for extended periods. He believes it restores their self-worth and confidence, helping them overcome violent tendencies. He considers his prison a model for other institutions looking to address the problem of violent prison gangs. 'It brought back their self esteem. We have happy inmates now -- we don't want to go back to the old jail where we had mad, sad inmates,' he said. In sweltering heat, 1,400 men in bright orange tracksuits flawlessly performed the 15-minute 'Thriller' routine. They had rehearsed for 10 hours the day before, concluding at 3 a.m. to rest before the show. The well-choreographed moves, energy, and enthusiasm of the prisoners captivated the audience, which included journalists from around the world. Several inmates even invited audience members to dance with them. 'I never thought I would ever find myself dancing with a prisoner,' one local resident exclaimed. A local journalist described the performance as Asia's best tribute to Jackson. Garcia, who claims the prison has been free of violence for three years, praised the performers: 'I'm so proud of them,' he said. 'They got the dance exactly right.' He added that he had hoped Michael Jackson would visit Cebu to dance and play the role himself, acknowledging that it was 'probably wishful thinking' and 'Now it's not going to happen,' he said mournfully. Convicted robber Mavin Cabido, 23, commented: 'I feel so sad as we idolize him really. The moonwalk is my favorite -- I like that.'

article_content: By Sam Peters. In the week FIFA was hit with a potentially crippling lawsuit over football’s ‘negligent’ handling of head injuries, the world governing body has launched a mental health research project. The class action suit, filed last Wednesday by a group of parents and players in California, alleges football’s governing body has acted ‘carelessly’ and ‘recklessly’ in its management of head injuries–a move which could have far-reaching implications for the sport. The filing reads: ‘FIFA presides over this [concussion] epidemic and is one of its primary causes.’ This summer’s World Cup in Brazil was marked by cases where players continued playing despite suspected concussions. Germany’s Christoph Kramer was eventually taken off in the final but initially kept playing. This summer’s World Cup in Brazil was marked by cases where players—including Germany’s Christoph Kramer in the final—were allowed to play on after suffering concussions. Last season’s Premier League also saw a number of concerning cases, one of which involved Tottenham goalkeeper Hugo Lloris, where medics were overruled by management eager to return players to the field. Earlier this month, the FA’s head of medicine, Dr. Ian Beasley, told the Mail on Sunday that football could face a ‘tsunami’ of damaging legal claims if it fails to radically improve its protocols. Beasley’s prediction appears to be coming true in the US. The so-called ‘soccer moms’ lawsuit is not seeking financial compensation but is looking for rule changes that allow adequate time for off-field assessment while limiting the number of headers allowed by children under 17. Symptoms such as depression, increased aggression levels, and increased risk of suicide have all been linked to repeated concussions, and FIFA’s investigation into mental health issues in football appears to be a response to the lawsuit. Tottenham goalkeeper Hugo Lloris overruled his medics and played on despite his injury. Lloris is led off by medical staff but returned to the action soon after and did not want to be substituted. Lloris, against his medical advisers' wishes, came back on the field after sustaining a head injury. ‘Any scientific data on the mental health of athletes is rare, and almost no scientific study has yet investigated the mental health among football players,’ the statement read. ‘To respond to this gap in knowledge, FIFA has established the new research area so that those in the game feel more comfortable coming forward to talk about issues and in order to ease access to treatment.’ Last week, a group of sports medics—including representatives from the NFL, FIFA, the International Rugby Board, and Australian Rules Football—met in New York to discuss what some have termed a ‘concussion crisis’. ‘FIFA’s decision to start research into mental health issues in the same week that a lawsuit is filed may be a coincidence,’ said one attendee. ‘There appears to be so little understanding of head injuries within the organization that they may not even have realized the link.’

article_content: Pictures have emerged showing the aftermath of a car crash involving David Beckham, in which his son Brooklyn was also present. The incident occurred after the former England football captain picked up his eldest son from Arsenal’s training ground on Saturday. Photos depict significant damage to the driver's side of Beckham's Audi RS6, while the other vehicle, identified as a Mitsubishi Colt Coupe Cabriolet, was reportedly written off. The accident happened after Beckham, 39, picked up Brooklyn from an Arsenal under-16s match north of London at the training centre in London Colney, Hertfordshire. He had been watching his son play against Brighton. Beckham reportedly received treatment at the scene for a minor shoulder injury, while Brooklyn was unharmed. A woman and her adult daughter in the other car were taken to hospital for minor injuries, according to The Sun. A witness told The Sun that Beckham was 'lucky to be alive' and reportedly gave his jumper to the woman from the other car while waiting for assistance. Arsenal staff directed onlookers away from the scene, and Beckham left in another vehicle. Both Beckhams were reportedly shaken by the incident. Following the accident, a Brighton player, Archie Davies, tweeted about seeing David Beckham and noting a possible shoulder injury. He later added that he was 'star struck' by the encounter. Another team-mate, Thomas Cadman, tweeted about playing against Brooklyn Beckham and then being stuck behind David Beckham after the car crash. Both David Beckham and Brooklyn walked away from the accident, with David sustaining a minor shoulder injury and Brooklyn remaining unhurt. Beckham's Audi RS6 sustained considerable damage. Despite the accident and reported shoulder injury, Beckham attended the Evening Standard Theatre Awards with his wife, Victoria, the following night. Airbags in Beckham's vehicle were reportedly deployed during the collision. This isn't Beckham's first car accident; in October of the previous year, he collided with another car while leaving his driveway in Beverly Hills. At that time, he was in his black Range Rover Sport with Brooklyn, then 14, in the front passenger seat. Damage was visible on both Beckham's Range Rover Sport and the other vehicle, a white Acura 4x4. Brooklyn signed a short-term contract with Arsenal earlier in the month after impressing coaches at The Emirates. His brother Romeo, 12, also plays for Arsenal’s under-13s, and their youngest son Cruz, 9, plays for the club’s under-10s. Brighton footballer Archie Davies tweeted about Beckham appearing injured after the crash, and then expressed being 'star struck' after seeing the former England international. Thomas Cadman, also a Brighton player, mentioned being stuck behind the Beckhams after the accident.

article_content: Rene Lecour had a straightforward idea: an 'epic' skateboarding adventure with his son, Kaya, in Cuba. After discovering videos of Cuban skateboarders improvising with damaged equipment online, the Lecours knew they had to visit. Cuba's economic struggles and the U.S. embargo significantly limit access to sporting goods, making it exceedingly difficult for skateboarders to obtain proper gear. 'We immediately knew we had to go,' Lecour remembered. Lecour, who runs a series of skateboarding stores in South Florida, believed his industry connections would make donating boards to Cuba easy. He was mistaken. 'I contacted every skateboard company I knew,' Lecour said. 'Sadly, one response claimed we shouldn't be allowed to go because of the embargo, while another 'genius' thought we shouldn't visit since all skaters are communists.' As a Cuban-American, Lecour had long wanted to see his parents' homeland. The Obama administration's eased travel rules made visits simpler for Cuban-Americans and those on cultural trips. But Lecour wanted to contribute meaningfully. The former DJ, covered in tattoos, spread the word that any skateboard, regardless of condition, would be appreciated by Cuban skaters. As his family prepared, skateboards gradually started arriving. 'The kids' reaction was incredible,' Lecour noted. 'A 9-year-old skater understands the need better than a 30-year-old skateboard company head who just doesn't get it.' A week before the Cuba trip, a donation party was held at a Miami skate park, complete with heavy metal music. As teenagers practiced tricks, more boards were added to Lecour's collection. 'This is truly amazing,' he said, realizing the impact of the journey. Cuban skaters like Che Alejandro Pando Napoles depend on support from people like Lecour. Pando explained that while skate parks exist in Cuba, skate shops don't. Skaters can't easily buy new boards or replace broken ones. 'It can hinder your progress,' Pando admitted. 'You might see a set of stairs and avoid doing a trick, wanting to protect your board rather than risk breaking it.' Skateboarding is Pando's life, highlighted by his wedding video showing him, his bride, and the wedding party skateboarding after the ceremony. Before Cuba, Lecour tried contacting Pando, a leading figure in Havana's skate scene. By chance, Lecour bumped into Pando shortly after arriving—a classic Havana moment. They quickly planned to skate and distribute the donated equipment. At Havana's Parque Metropolitano, Lecour saw numerous skaters, realizing he hadn't brought enough. Pando reassured him they would organize a skate competition. The Americans watched in awe as the Cuban skaters performed tricks with limited equipment. Lecour, his wife Yirka, son Kaya, and friend Shane were amazed. 'I don't know how he manages with such small wheels,' Lecour commented. The competition ended, and although most skaters didn't win boards, they were happy with the hats, shirts, and sunglasses. The board winners beamed with joy. Lecour insisted he wasn't trying to be a 'savior.' 'The Cuban skaters have been so welcoming, inviting us to meals and gatherings,' he said. 'I'm already planning my next trip and what equipment I'll bring.'

article_content: In Washington, a House committee hearing transformed into a contentious public argument, punctuated by Republican Chairman Darrell Issa's decision to silence microphones while a leading Democrat attempted to speak. Following Wednesday's chaotic events, Issa acknowledged that the almost year-long inquiry into the Internal Revenue Service's alleged targeting of conservative organizations might be nearing its conclusion. 'It's quite possible that we've reached the end of the road,' Issa told reporters after Lois Lerner, a former IRS manager, again declined to testify before the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, citing her Fifth Amendment rights. An aide to Issa indicated that the committee chairman hadn't yet decided whether to pursue contempt charges against Lerner. This uncertainty brings up the question of whether Republicans, who assert that the targeting directive originated from higher-ups in the political sphere, potentially even within the White House, can successfully win a legal challenge to force Lerner to provide testimony. 'Without that, the probe might end with Ms. Lerner,' Issa commented. Republicans argue that the IRS subjected groups seeking tax-exempt status to increased scrutiny for political reasons, specifically targeting organizations with 'tea party' and other conservative-leaning terms in their names. The IRS, the Obama administration, and Democrats refute any political intent, pointing out that liberal groups also faced additional examination due to their names. Lerner, who was placed on administrative leave and subsequently retired from the IRS last year, headed the department responsible for the screening. To date, she has consistently refused to testify before Congress on this matter, as she did again Wednesday before the committee led by Issa. Issa's actions sparked outrage, as he has been leading a Republican investigation that has so far failed to uncover any political motivations behind the targeting. Issa adjourned Wednesday's session over the protests of Democratic Rep. Elijah Cummings of Maryland, who retorted that the chairman's actions were 'absolutely un-American.' As Cummings demanded to be heard, Issa announced, 'We've adjourned,' and gestured to the committee to cut off the microphones. Cummings continued to speak loudly, compensating for the lack of amplification. 'I am a member of the Congress of the United States of America. I am tired of this,' Cummings exclaimed. 'You can't just conduct a one-sided investigation. There's definitely something wrong with that.' Afterward, Issa explained to reporters that the hearing's objective was to determine if Lerner would waive her Fifth Amendment rights and answer questions. Once it became apparent that she wouldn't, there was no justification for continuing, according to the chairman from California. 'Mr. Cummings didn't raise a point of privilege or a point or order,' Issa stated, noting that he initially recognized Cummings for a question. 'He transitioned into an opening statement, and opening statements had already concluded.' When pressed further, Issa explained that he had the microphones turned off because Cummings persisted in speaking during 'an adjourned meeting.' 'He was actually defaming me when the microphones were cut off, claiming that this hadn't been a legitimate investigation,' Issa complained. Cummings asserted that the issue centered on allowing Democrats on the committee to express their views. 'We were essentially completely excluded,' he told reporters, criticizing Issa and Republicans for consistently distorting the committee's conclusions by 'selectively extracting information, sending just a few lines from various transcripts.'

Após os eventos turbulentos de quarta-feira, Issa admitiu que a investigação de quase um ano sobre o suposto direcionamento de organizações conservadoras pelo Internal Revenue Service (IRS) pode estar se aproximando de um impasse. 'É bem possível que tenhamos chegado ao fim da linha', disse Issa aos jornalistas após Lois Lerner, ex-gerente do IRS, ter se recusado novamente a testemunhar perante o Comitê de Supervisão e Reforma Governamental da Câmara, invocando seus direitos da Quinta Emenda. Um assessor de Issa indicou que o presidente do comitê ainda não havia tomado uma decisão sobre se buscaria acusações de desacato contra Lerner. Essa incerteza levanta dúvidas sobre se os republicanos, que alegam que a ordem de direcionamento se originou de figuras superiores na esfera política, possivelmente até mesmo dentro da Casa Branca, podem vencer uma batalha legal para obrigar Lerner a depor. 'Sem isso, a investigação pode terminar na Sra. Lerner', observou Issa. O IRS, o governo Obama e os democratas negam qualquer motivação política, ressaltando que grupos de orientação liberal também foram submetidos a exames adicionais devido aos seus nomes. Lerner, que foi colocada em licença administrativa e posteriormente se aposentou do IRS no ano passado, liderava a unidade responsável pela triagem. Até o momento, ela tem se recusado consistentemente a testemunhar perante o Congresso sobre o assunto, como fez novamente na quarta-feira perante o comitê presidido por Issa. As ações de Issa provocaram indignação, já que ele lidera uma investigação republicana que até agora não conseguiu descobrir nenhuma motivação política por trás do direcionamento. Issa encerrou a sessão de quarta-feira em meio aos protestos do deputado democrata Elijah Cummings, de Maryland, que rebateu que as ações do presidente eram 'absolutamente antiamericanas'. 'Sou um membro do Congresso dos Estados Unidos da América. Estou farto disso', exclamou Cummings. 'Não se pode simplesmente conduzir uma investigação unilateral. Há algo fundamentalmente errado nisso.' Uma vez que ficou claro que ela não o faria, não havia justificativa para prosseguir, de acordo com o presidente da Califórnia. 'O Sr. Cummings não levantou uma questão de ordem ou uma questão de privilégio', afirmou Issa, observando que ele inicialmente havia concedido a palavra a Cummings para uma pergunta. 'Ele passou a fazer uma declaração inicial, e as declarações iniciais já haviam sido concluídas.' Quando questionado mais a fundo, Issa explicou que mandou desligar os microfones porque Cummings persistiu em falar durante 'uma sessão encerrada'. 'Ele estava, na verdade, me difamando no momento em que os microfones foram cortados, alegando que esta não tinha sido uma investigação legítima', queixou-se Issa. Cummings alegou que a questão central era permitir que os democratas na comissão expressassem seus pontos de vista. 'Fomos essencialmente excluídos por completo', disse ele aos repórteres, criticando Issa e os republicanos por distorcerem consistentemente as conclusões da comissão, 'selecionando informações de forma tendenciosa, enviando apenas algumas linhas de várias transcrições'.

article_content: By Jonathan McEvoy for the Daily Mail. Lewis Hamilton's possible return to McLaren moved a step closer when his former boss, Ron Dennis, hinted he is considering re-signing his former protégé. McLaren are waiting to see how the strained relationship between Hamilton and Nico Rosberg unfolds at Mercedes, with the British driver on a shortlist of three star drivers that also includes Fernando Alonso and Sebastian Vettel. 'No one could have predicted the tension inside Mercedes-Benz,' said Dennis. 'We can all imagine a range of scenarios that could see one of those drivers on the market by the end of the year.' Return: Lewis Hamilton could be in line for a return to McLaren after a difficult period with Mercedes. Dennis, who is famous for 'Ron-speak' – his circumlocutory style of expression – added: 'You are trying to understand what is available, and then you make a decision.' It is understood that preliminary talks between McLaren representatives and Hamilton's representatives have taken place. Eric Boullier, McLaren's racing director, is even more eager to sign Hamilton than Dennis, who had a falling out with the driver towards the end of his time with the team. With Alonso, McLaren's primary target, having last week reiterated his desire to stay at Ferrari, Hamilton is a strong contender to take the place of either Jenson Button or Kevin Magnussen, the two current McLaren drivers. Pole: Hamilton edged out his Mercedes teammate, Nico Rosberg, to take pole at the Italian Grand Prix. It would be a bold move for Hamilton to leave Mercedes, one of the best-funded and fastest teams in the sport, but his potential disillusionment could be so strong if he were to lose the title that he might feel the urge to leave. There is also the possibility that Mercedes could part ways with him to end the tense rivalry between Hamilton and Rosberg. Even though Mercedes have tried to manage their warring drivers, team boss Toto Wolff warned this week that they could suspend or sack either of them if there was any repeat of their collision at the last race in Spa a fortnight ago. 'We would have to make decisions and face the consequences of having a different lineup,' he said. 'If we are not able to manage the two of them following the Mercedes-Benz spirit, then we need to admit that.' Feud: The relationship between Mercedes drivers Hamilton and Rosberg has deteriorated significantly.

article_content: After two decades, authorities are revisiting the case of Jennifer Odom, a 12-year-old who vanished in 1993 in rural Brooksville, Florida. Her body was discovered six days later on a nearby horse trail. Detectives plan to reanalyze all physical evidence using modern DNA technology. Initial investigations, including a feature on 'Unsolved Mysteries' and a $20,000 reward, failed to identify the killer. Now, Hernando County Sheriff's Detective Jim Boylan, leading the cold case division, pledges a meticulous examination of every detail. They will also scrutinize convicted serial killers who might have been in the region at the time. The FBI is assisting by providing data to potentially link the crime to individuals from outside Florida. Boylan notes the case profoundly affected the community. Madeline Beaumont, a local resident who participated in the search, recalls widespread fear following Jennifer's disappearance. Hernando County Sheriff Al Neinhuis has assigned a full-time detective to the case, funded by a grant. Additionally, civilian volunteers will conduct a comprehensive review of all documents and evidence. Authorities have received thousands of tips over the years, with more arriving since the sheriff's announcement. Some tips point to possible leads in Ohio and Pennsylvania, though specifics remain undisclosed. Evidence suggests the perpetrator was familiar with the area. While the person's current whereabouts are unknown, Boylan does not necessarily believe they are still local. Boylan supervises 20 unsolved cases, including missing persons and homicides. Jennifer's case is unique as she is the only child involved. Jennifer's family reported nothing unusual leading up to her disappearance on February 19, 1993. Her sister, Jessica, found the door locked when she arrived home that day and alerted their parents. A community search ensued, but Jennifer's body was found on a horse trail in Hernando County six days later. Identification was made through a gold chain and fingerprints. The cause of death has not been released. Jennifer's mother, Renee Converse, expressed the difficulty of accepting her death without seeing her body. She was unavailable for current comment. Witnesses reported seeing a light blue pickup truck near the bus stop on the day of the disappearance. Investigators are keen to speak with the occupant(s) of the truck, believing they may have valuable information. Two years later, Jennifer's book bag and clarinet were found concealed in the woods, suggesting the killer was familiar with the local area. Anyone with information is urged to contact Hernando County Crimestoppers at 866-990-8477 or Detective Jim Boylan at 352-797-3719.

article_content: A couple from Rochdale, Greater Manchester, John Leigh, aged 54, and Deborah Hancox, aged 45, have been imprisoned for a combined total of five and a half years after stealing £1 million from the National Health Service. The stolen funds were used to finance a luxurious lifestyle filled with international travel and expensive vehicles. Over a seven-year period, Leigh and Hancox conspired to provide the NHS with equipment and services at highly inflated prices. The fraud is believed to have exceeded £1 million, with the couple personally gaining approximately £300,000, which they invested in vacation properties in Cyprus, Dubai, and the Lake District. The pair also acquired a brand-new Jaguar convertible and a Mercedes-Benz using the illicit proceeds. They admitted guilt to charges of conspiracy to defraud and concealing criminal assets during an earlier court appearance at Manchester Crown Court, which led to their sentencing. Leigh received a prison sentence of 44 months, while Hancox was sentenced to 24 months. Their apprehension followed a five-year search that began after police questioned them about the fraud in 2008, after which they absconded to the Turkish region of Cyprus. They were only returned to England last year to face legal proceedings after relocating to the southern part of the island, known as the Republic of Cyprus. Leigh's position within the NHS purchasing department allowed him to primarily acquire computers and other office supplies for various NHS departments. Hancox, his partner, was also an NHS employee. For more than seven years, Leigh utilized a company named Action Direct Technology Ltd, owned and directed by Hancox, to purchase overpriced goods, thereby defrauding the NHS. The couple further employed Bibi's IT Solutions Ltd and Wiscom Technology Ltd as fronts to conceal their ongoing fraudulent activities between January 2001 and October 2008. According to Sgt Laura Walters of GMP, the couple engaged in a meticulously planned and executed conspiracy to defraud the NHS of hundreds of thousands of pounds. This wasn't a quick money-making scheme but a sustained criminal operation that spanned seven years. Despite the length of time, they displayed no regret for their actions. It is believed that the reason they switched companies later was an attempt to hide their actions should an investigation ever occur. Hundreds of email exchanges were seized, showing their elaborate attempts to cover their tracks by manipulating financial records to create an illusion of legitimacy. The proceeds from their criminal activity were clearly used to support a lavish lifestyle, including a holiday home in the Lake District and property investments in the United Arab Emirates and Cyprus. This crime should not be considered victimless, as the NHS was defrauded of funds urgently needed for treating genuinely ill individuals. Every penny stolen represents money diverted from those in critical need of medical care. Sgt Walters expressed her delight that the case had concluded, and the con artists had been exposed and brought to justice. Sue Frith, managing director of NHS Protect, stated that this was a serious fraud against the NHS, perpetrated by individuals who abused their positions of trust and authority. Their attempts to evade justice compounded their crimes. NHS Protect will pursue all fraud suspicions and investigate them appropriately. They will press for prosecution and seek the strongest sanctions to ensure public money is used for patient care.
translated_content: Um casal de Rochdale, Grande Manchester, John Leigh, de 54 anos, e Deborah Hancox, de 45 anos, foi preso por um total combinado de cinco anos e meio após roubar £1 milhão do Serviço Nacional de Saúde (NHS). Os fundos roubados foram usados para financiar um estilo de vida luxuoso, cheio de viagens internacionais e veículos caros. Ao longo de um período de sete anos, Leigh e Hancox conspiraram para fornecer ao NHS equipamentos e serviços a preços altamente inflacionados. Acredita-se que a fraude tenha excedido £1 milhão, com o casal ganhando pessoalmente aproximadamente £300.000, que investiram em propriedades de férias em Chipre, Dubai e no Lake District. O casal também adquiriu um Jaguar conversível novo e uma Mercedes-Benz usando os lucros ilícitos. Eles se declararam culpados das acusações de conspiração para fraudar e ocultar ativos criminais durante uma audiência judicial anterior no Tribunal da Coroa de Manchester, o que levou à sua condenação. Leigh recebeu uma sentença de prisão de 44 meses, enquanto Hancox foi sentenciada a 24 meses. A sua apreensão ocorreu após uma busca de cinco anos que começou depois que a polícia os interrogou sobre a fraude em 2008, após o que eles fugiram para a região turca de Chipre. Eles só foram devolvidos à Inglaterra no ano passado para enfrentar processos legais depois de se mudarem para a parte sul da ilha, conhecida como República de Chipre. A posição de Leigh no departamento de compras do NHS permitiu-lhe adquirir principalmente computadores e outros materiais de escritório para vários departamentos do NHS. Hancox, sua parceira, também era funcionária do NHS. Por mais de sete anos, Leigh utilizou uma empresa chamada Action Direct Technology Ltd, propriedade e dirigida por Hancox, para comprar mercadorias superfaturadas, fraudando assim o NHS. O casal também empregou a Bibi's IT Solutions Ltd e a Wiscom Technology Ltd como fachadas para ocultar as suas atividades fraudulentas em curso entre janeiro de 2001 e outubro de 2008. De acordo com a Sgt. Laura Walters da GMP, o casal envolveu-se numa conspiração meticulosamente planeada e executada para fraudar o NHS em centenas de milhares de libras. Este não foi um esquema rápido para ganhar dinheiro, mas uma operação criminosa sustentada que durou sete anos. Apesar do tempo decorrido, não demonstraram arrependimento pelas suas ações. Acredita-se que a razão pela qual mudaram de empresa mais tarde foi uma tentativa de esconder as suas ações caso alguma vez ocorresse uma investigação. Centenas de trocas de e-mail foram apreendidas, mostrando as suas elaboradas tentativas de encobrir os seus rastos, manipulando os registos financeiros para criar uma ilusão de legitimidade. Os proventos da sua atividade criminosa foram claramente usados para sustentar um estilo de vida luxuoso, incluindo uma casa de férias no Lake District e investimentos imobiliários nos Emirados Árabes Unidos e em Chipre. Este crime não deve ser considerado sem vítimas, pois o NHS foi fraudado de fundos urgentemente necessários para tratar indivíduos genuinamente doentes. Cada cêntimo roubado representa dinheiro desviado daqueles que necessitam urgentemente de cuidados médicos. A Sgt. Walters expressou a sua satisfação pelo facto de o caso ter sido concluído e de os burlões terem sido expostos e levados à justiça. Sue Frith, diretora-gerente da NHS Protect, afirmou que esta foi uma fraude grave contra o NHS, perpetrada por indivíduos que abusaram das suas posições de confiança e autoridade. As suas tentativas de evasão à justiça agravaram os seus crimes. A NHS Protect irá investigar todas as suspeitas de fraude e investigá-las adequadamente. Insistirão na acusação e procurarão as sanções mais fortes para garantir que o dinheiro público seja usado para os cuidados ao paciente.

article_content: Kabul, Afghanistan (CNN) -- Because no candidate secured over half the votes, Afghanistan's presidential election will proceed to a second round, as announced by the nation's election commission on Saturday. The leading candidates, Abdullah Abdullah, previously the Foreign Minister, and Ashraf Ghani, will compete in a runoff election scheduled for June 7, according to Ahmad Yusuf Nuristani, head of the Independent Election Commission. 'I believe the elections went quite well. We're happy with both the process and the outcome,' Nuristani stated on national television. On April 5, seven million Afghans voted to elect a replacement for current President Hamid Karzai. This event marks the country's first democratic presidential power transition. The preliminary results revealed Abdullah with 45% of the votes and Ghani with 32%. Zalmai Rasoul's presidential bid ended with a third-place finish, capturing 12% of the vote. Abdullah and Ghani were considered the frontrunners as they entered the April 5 ballot. Abdullah, linked to the Tajik ethnic group, is partnered with Mohammad Mohaqeq, a prominent Hazara ethnic group leader. Additionally, his ticket includes a Pashtun representative. Trained as an ophthalmologist, Abdullah previously served as Afghanistan's foreign minister under Karzai. He contested against Karzai in 2009 but withdrew, citing concerns about widespread voter fraud. He is generally seen as a liberal figure and has publicly voiced his support for women's rights. Ghani, a Columbia University doctorate recipient, belongs to the Pashtun ethnic group. His running mate is Abdul Rashid Dostum, a leader within the Uzbek ethnic group. Ghani formerly held the position of finance minister under Karzai. For the next president, maintaining security is a major concern. The lead-up to the election was marred by a series of deadly incidents, and violence struck Kabul again on Thursday when a policeman guarding a hospital shot and killed at least three American medical professionals. NATO forces are scheduled to withdraw from Afghanistan by year's end. Karzai, constitutionally limited to two terms, has declined to sign the Status of Forces Agreement, which would keep international forces in Afghanistan. However, both leading presidential contenders have indicated they would sign the agreement.
translated_content: Cabul, Afeganistão (CNN) -- Como nenhum candidato obteve mais da metade dos votos, a eleição presidencial do Afeganistão irá para o segundo turno, conforme anunciado pela comissão eleitoral do país no sábado. Os principais candidatos, Abdullah Abdullah, anteriormente Ministro das Relações Exteriores, e Ashraf Ghani, competirão num segundo turno agendado para 7 de junho, de acordo com Ahmad Yusuf Nuristani, chefe da Comissão Eleitoral Independente. 'Acredito que as eleições correram muito bem. Estamos felizes tanto com o processo quanto com o resultado', afirmou Nuristani na televisão nacional. Em 5 de abril, sete milhões de afegãos votaram para eleger um substituto para o atual presidente Hamid Karzai. Este evento marca a primeira transição democrática de poder presidencial do país. Os resultados preliminares revelaram Abdullah com 45% dos votos e Ghani com 32%. A candidatura presidencial de Zalmai Rasoul terminou com um terceiro lugar, capturando 12% dos votos. Abdullah e Ghani eram considerados os favoritos ao entrarem na votação de 5 de abril. Abdullah, ligado ao grupo étnico Tajique, está em parceria com Mohammad Mohaqeq, um proeminente líder do grupo étnico Hazara. Além disso, a sua chapa inclui um representante Pashtun. Formado como oftalmologista, Abdullah já atuou como ministro das Relações Exteriores do Afeganistão sob Karzai. Ele concorreu contra Karzai em 2009, mas retirou-se, citando preocupações com fraude eleitoral generalizada. Ele é geralmente visto como uma figura liberal e expressou publicamente o seu apoio aos direitos das mulheres. Ghani, doutorado pela Universidade de Columbia, pertence ao grupo étnico Pashtun. O seu companheiro de chapa é Abdul Rashid Dostum, um líder dentro do grupo étnico Uzbeque. Ghani ocupou anteriormente o cargo de ministro das Finanças sob Karzai. Para o próximo presidente, manter a segurança é uma grande preocupação. A preparação para a eleição foi marcada por uma série de incidentes mortais, e a violência atingiu Cabul novamente na quinta-feira, quando um polícia que guardava um hospital atirou e matou pelo menos três profissionais médicos americanos. As forças da OTAN devem retirar-se do Afeganistão até o final do ano. Karzai, constitucionalmente limitado a dois mandatos, recusou-se a assinar o Acordo sobre o Status das Forças, que manteria as forças internacionais no Afeganistão. No entanto, ambos os principais candidatos presidenciais indicaram que assinariam o acordo.

article_content: Although quite different individuals, Brian May and Sir Patrick Moore shared a scientific connection. Their bond was so profound that May acquired Moore's residence to guarantee his lifelong occupancy. In 2008, Brian bought 'Farthings', the Selsey, West Sussex home, for £480,000. He exceeded the market value by about £40,000, ensuring the astronomer could remain in his home of four decades. Sir Patrick Moore passed away peacefully at his home recently at the age of 89. Brian leased the property back to Moore the same day of purchase for a nominal fee, as reported by The Sunday Times. The lease was for 25 years at 'one peppercorn if demanded'. The Queen guitarist expressed outrage on his website regarding The Sunday Times' story. He stated, 'Sir Patrick Moore isn't even buried, and The Sunday Times is already snooping around to 'reveal' details about how his friends assisted him in his final years.' May further commented on the intrusiveness of the press, questioning their lack of respect for private matters. Sir Patrick Moore had a passion for the xylophone. May told The Guardian that deciding the house's future is premature, but indicated that Moore's scientific collection could be publicly accessible. May, whose net worth is estimated at £90m, regarded Sir Patrick as a 'father figure' who inspired him to pursue a PhD in astrophysics. He admired Moore since childhood, staying up late to watch 'The Sky At Night'. Their connection strengthened after a radio play collaboration and co-authoring 'Bang! The Complete History of the Universe'. They also shared a love for music. Moore was a self-taught xylophone player with a strict rule at Farthings: no one was to touch the xylophone. Moore composed over 100 musical pieces, including a march dedicated to Halley’s Comet. He even recognized one of his Viennese waltzes playing on his car radio. Moore was a prominent social figure, frequently hosting parties in Selsey with Brian May and his wife, Anita Dobson. Sir Patrick initially acquired Farthings for £4,000 cash in 1967. It also housed his personal observatory. Moore specified that he wanted a party, not a funeral, to celebrate his life. His friends and family intend to honor this wish. Eventually, he had four observatories in his backyard but they were damaged during a storm in 1998. Finances were not always stable, as he prioritized telescopes, parties, and assisting young astronomers. Neighbor Eileen Nolan mentioned the accountant frequently limiting Moore's spending. Brian May offered assistance if Moore faced financial difficulties, often providing support. In an obituary, May highlighted Moore's generosity towards young astronomers and his willingness to give away his income, depending on friends for security.
